topics.body:
Advance Marin's isolated external runtimes to the current commits on their configured branches.

The updated MarinSkyRL schema rejects the ingress block and retired generator transport settings. Marin's launch recipes now omit those fields so pinned async RL and Cat Count launches compose under the new schema.

| Project | Distribution | Version | Commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `evalchemy` | `evalchemy` | `0.1.0` | [`97fffeb7df60`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/97fffeb7df60875c5a5c14ec215dd4e7683102c5) |
| `MarinSkyRL` | `marinskyrl` | `0.1.0` | [`c96f6d25f599`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/c96f6d25f59959096c3b179a51e67c0af6c99536) |

## Upstream commits

### evalchemy (`2083afa0b937` → `97fffeb7df60`)

- [`7a11ea7c1ea6`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/7a11ea7c1ea6b7c0cbfcf6bb85aae181c3325408): [graders] Zero empty candidates before the judge (#206)

topics.title: [haliax] Add Pallas-Triton tile-map ragged_dot kernels for AMD GPUs
topics.body:
On AMD Instinct GPUs, `ragged_dot(..., implementation="triton")` now runs a second family of Pallas-Triton grouped-GEMM kernels, called tile-map kernels. NVIDIA GPUs, TPU and megablox behave exactly as before. NVIDIA keeps the existing group-grid kernels and block sizes, including the Blackwell `block_n` of 256. Those kernels are unchanged in the diff. `_TILE_MAP_GPU_FAMILIES` lists the GPU families that use the tile-map kernels. Adding NVIDIA to it is a one-line change, for a follow-up once H100 and B200 have been measured.

These kernels use Pallas-Triton, which JAX 0.11 deprecates; Mosaic GPU, the replacement JAX suggests, does not support ROCm. #9859 ports the same kernels to Triton launched through `jax_triton.triton_call`, but jax-triton kernels hang multi-GPU training on ROCm today. On a kernel's first launch, jaxlib 0.11.1 reads the compiled hsaco from a temporary file and deletes it without holding its cache lock, so when the 8 GPUs of one process launch together, all but one fail and the step stalls at the next collective (evidence in #9859). This PR lands the Pallas-Triton version so AMD runs can use the tile-map kernels now. #9859 replaces them once a jaxlib release fixes the race.

The existing kernels give every group a full grid over all row tiles and exit early on most of them. In the tile-map kernels, the forward and input-gradient (dlhs) kernels launch one program per (group, row tile, column tile) from a tile map built on device from `group_sizes`, as in megablox's `make_group_metadata`. dlhs reads the weights transposed in place, with no `rhs.mT` copy. The weight gradient (drhs) uses one flat grid over all groups. Rows past `sum(group_sizes)` are zero-filled. The old kernels leave them unwritten. Block sizes come from a per-GPU-family table that was swept on MI350X. Two launch-order options are new: chiplet-aware program numbering (`num_xcds`) and grouped tile rows (`group_m`).

Per-call times on one MI350X, bf16, balanced groups. Each cell is TFLOP/s for the old kernels, then the new ones (job 453824). The June expert shapes are G=32, with w13 at K=N=2560 and w2 at K=1280, N=2560.

| Shape | M | fwd | dlhs | drhs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| June w13 | 16384 | 94 → 594 | 88 → 635 | 378 → 483 |
| June w13 | 131072 | 587 → 730 | 556 → 808 | 428 → 585 |
| June w13 | 196608 | 525 → 735 | 511 → 818 | 429 → 579 |
| June w2 | 131072 | 560 → 668 | 541 → 765 | 403 → 586 |
| Mixtral-like w1, G=8, 4096x14336 | 16384 | 425 → 771 | 383 → 861 | 435 → 593 |
| Mixtral-like w1 | 65536 | 629 → 792 | 596 → 898 | 449 → 591 |

A dense `jnp.matmul` with the same FLOPs runs at about 730-960 TFLOP/s on this GPU. A sweep of `group_m` from 1 to 16 and `num_xcds` of 1 or 8 ran at both shape sets. Every setting beat the old kernels, and the chosen AMD entries are within 5% of the best setting sampled.

The full June model ran on 8x MI350X with EP8, `gpu_pallas_triton_flash` attention, memory fraction 0.90 and 20 steps. The table gives the median step over steps 2-19:

| Remat | Batch | Old kernels | New kernels | Peak memory (new) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| recompute_all | 64 | 2.149 s (122.0k tok/s) | 1.853 s (141.5k tok/s) | 158.4 GiB |
| recompute_all | 96 | 3.080 s (127.7k tok/s) | 2.696 s (145.9k tok/s) | 164.7 GiB |
| save_moe | 64 | 1.988 s (131.9k tok/s) | 1.832 s (143.1k tok/s) | 205.8 GiB |
| save_moe | 96 | 2.867 s (137.2k tok/s) | 2.672 s (147.2k tok/s) | 235.7 GiB |

Step-19 loss agrees with the old kernels within 1e-4. Earlier batch-96 runs on these kernels took 4.5-5.0 s per step, and one ran out of memory. Those runs reused XLA autotuning results from the per-fusion autotune cache, which JAX keeps inside `--compilation-cache-dir`. With that cache off (`JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ENABLE_XLA_CACHES=none`) or empty, batch 96 runs at 2.66-2.70 s and its throughput is above batch 64. The kernels were not the cause: per call they are 25-35% faster at batch 96's M=196608. With a warm autotune cache, save_moe at batch 64 took 4.95 s per step on the new kernels and 5.62 s on the old ones. With fresh autotuning it took 1.83 s and 1.99 s. Jobs: 453914, 453961 and 453944 (A/B), 453791 and 453823 (cache reproduction).

The per-call numbers and the block-size sweep came from `lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_ragged_dot_triton.py`, which is in #9894. The edge-case tests (empty groups, unaligned boundaries, rows past the last group, partial tiles, every VJP layout) run for both families on a GPU. The tile-map family also runs them on CPU through the Pallas interpreter. Tests passed on MI350X (job 453882) and on the CPU interpreter (job 453881), and again after rebasing onto current main: all 72 on MI350X (job 458117), and on MI300X 42 passed with the 30 f32 cases skipped (job 458116). f32 cases skip on NVIDIA and on gfx942 (MI300X, MI325X), because Triton runs f32 dots in TF32 there. `test_accelerator_implementation_value_and_gradients_match_xla` now runs at highest matmul precision, as #9922 did for the custom VJP test: at default precision, XLA's autotuner on MI300X decides per process whether f32 dots run in xf32, and the test failed in 3 of 5 MI300X runs. With the change it passed 10 of 10 (job 458222).

Background and earlier measurements: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6027367267

Part of #9812

topics.title: [iris] Renew worker credentials before expiry
topics.body:
Renew worker credentials one day before their 30-day expiry, including while workers are idle, and persist replacements across process restarts. Restrict renewal to authenticated workers and admins; expired credentials still require operator recovery. Controllers refresh provisioning credentials, and manual worker creation and restart obtain fresh tokens from the controller.

An expired worker token could remain unnoticed while the log client reused a cached Finelog endpoint. After a timeout invalidated that cache, controller endpoint discovery rejected the token and log batches were discarded even though tasks continued running. The October 9 audit found expired credentials on six CPU workers; targeted credential replacement and process restarts restored central logging without restarting their seven task containers.

Deploy the controller renewal RPC before the worker changes. Worker tokens remain shared identities without individual revocation; a stolen token can also renew itself.

[Incident diagnosis and recovery](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/691).

topics.title: [grug] Add a Pallas-Triton flash attention for AMD GPUs
topics.body:
Add `gpu_pallas_triton_flash`, an opt-in fused causal attention for Grug on AMD GPUs, where Grug has no fused kernel. Existing backends are unchanged.

These kernels use Pallas-Triton, which JAX 0.11 deprecates; Mosaic GPU, the replacement JAX suggests for Pallas, does not support ROCm. #9853 ports the same kernels to Triton launched through `jax_triton.triton_call`, 12-24% faster per layer on MI300X and MI350X, but jax-triton kernels hang multi-GPU training on ROCm today. On a kernel's first launch, jaxlib 0.11.1 reads the compiled hsaco from a temporary file and deletes it without holding its cache lock, so when the 8 GPUs of one process launch together, all but one fail and the step stalls at the next collective (evidence and a standalone repro in #9853). This PR lands the Pallas-Triton version so AMD runs can use fused attention now. #9853 replaces it once AMD's jax fork, which builds the ROCm plugin, fixes the race.

The kernel reduces each mask to one inclusive key lower bound per query, `max(segment start, q - W + 1)` for window `W`. Key blocks outside `[lower bound, q]` are skipped, and blocks fully inside it skip the mask computation. GQA indexes the shared KV head instead of repeating K/V. Under a mesh, batch and heads may be sharded; sequence and head_dim may not. The lower bounds are computed here and not with the FA4/CuTe helpers, which treat negative segment IDs as padding and would make the ROCm path import the CuTe backend.

One layer's forward plus backward at the June per-GPU shape (8 x 4096 tokens, 20 query heads, 5 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16), median of three interleaved rounds in one process, jax 0.11.1 (jobs 457836, 457837):

| Mask | GPU | reference | `gpu_pallas_triton_flash` |
|---|---|---|---|
| window 2048 | MI350X | 20.19 ms | 6.77 ms |
| causal | MI350X | 22.26 ms | 10.04 ms |
| window 2048 | MI300X | 31.17 ms | 12.04 ms |
| causal | MI300X | 32.32 ms | 17.28 ms |

The full June model at batch 64 on 8x MI350X goes from 2.426 s to 1.853 s per step (9.32% to 12.20% MFU) with jaxlib 0.11.0, peak memory falls from 184 to 158 GiB, and the loss matches the reference run (https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6027803714).

Value and gradient parity tests against `reference_attention` pass on MI350X (job 458164) and in the Pallas interpreter on CPU (job 458155), which is the only way CI runs them. On MI300X the bf16 cases pass and the f32 cases skip (job 458163): Triton runs the kernels' default-precision f32 dots in TF32 on gfx942 and NVIDIA GPUs, about 2.7e-3 off the f32 reference.

Each run of equal segment IDs is one document, so a segment ID that reappears after a different ID starts a new document; `reference_attention` lets the two runs attend to each other. Masks that carry FA4 precomputed bounds are rejected, which excludes the moe_hero_ep, moe_hero_fsdp and fast_track variants.

Part of #9812

topics.body:
Stage the immutable vLLM 0.30 candidate for H100 and GB200 with Torch 2.14.1 and CUDA 13.2. Both wheels come from shared fork source `47b411d5785d1c3dee0328334472d70310c53feb`. The normal Marin installer uses the candidate's architecture-specific dependency constraints and matching NVCC, CCCL and NVRTC components.

Add size-one `expert` and `context` dimensions to the Levanter serving mesh. Snowball's weight layout requires these names; their absence failed scoring after the model loaded. The dimensions preserve the existing data and tensor-parallel sizes. The numerical CPU regression reproduces the failure before the fix, then compares logits from the same weights on the canonical Snowball training mesh and the serving mesh.

Snowball's 64 representative cases passed on 8 H100s with Levanter and on 8 and 16 H100s with vLLM. The unchanged bounds on absolute token-probability differences are 0.075 for Levanter and 0.125 for vLLM. The largest logged differences were 0.056754, 0.059786 and 0.055632, respectively. The normal installer and a transport smoke check of brokered Qwen3-0.6B completions also passed on one H100. These results cover Marin's standalone Transformers 5.18 profile.

Snowball and Hero passed fresh training, checkpoint restoration and HF export on H100 and GB200 in MarinSkyRL's combined training and serving profile (Transformers 5.12.1). Hero/GB200's driver finished successfully before a worker pod was deleted during shutdown; four queued worker retries for that completed run were canceled.

On matched inputs at batch 128 and context 4096, Hero's GB200 policy-update benchmark took 56.37 seconds with the refreshed [dependency profile](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/c9def79c0ac7d043879c669722aab311532b3b03/uv.lock) (Torch 2.14.1) versus 48.10 seconds with the shipping [dependency profile](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/f85737fc366d1f077ce9216b179a2a98a0bf8d14/uv.lock) (Torch 2.13.0), 17.2% longer. Peak GPU allocation was effectively unchanged. Several dependencies differ between these profiles; the cause remains unresolved. This performance regression is unaccepted.

Keep this draft pending official release qualification and protected promotion. The pinned wheels are staged in [marin-vllm-gpu-staged-candidate-47b411d5785d](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-staged-candidate-47b411d5785d). Rollback is GPU release `marin-vllm-gpu-20260924-01911be34fac`, source `01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e`. The [paired TPU refresh](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10023) uses a separate dependency environment. The [admin promotion handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10022#issuecomment-6093743002) records the remaining release gates, source promotion order and rollback refs.

Stage vLLM 0.30 source `47b411d5785d1c3dee0328334472d70310c53feb` with tpu-inference 0.30 source `66c5d8952eec0c263361915cb4613d8f30737955`. GPU and TPU use the same vLLM source and separate dependency environments. Stack this adoption on the [GPU candidate adoption](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10022).

Two fresh source and native build environments produced byte-identical complete TPU wheels with the pinned Debian GCC 12.2 recipe. The [normal GitHub producer](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/actions/runs/38083919768) atomically published the [exact pair](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-tpu-candidate-47b411d5785d-66c5d8952eec-aa04b4969cf2-309096c4b1e9). Independently downloaded archives match the agreed vLLM SHA256 `c45de5c1322343b7b6953ae791aa56029c8254ce60e90c1ef4866dc670249bae` and backend SHA256 `dedad6b56c6fd01716bfa148b72cc2e32080eccf68b403d810748569408ab2e6`. A clean Linux installation passed the 240-package dependency check and imported the native modules `vllm.spinloop` and `vllm.fs_io_C`.

TPU runtime remains unqualified. The backend scheduler imports `vllm.distributed.aux_output_connector`, which is absent from the selected shared vLLM source. Substantial API porting belongs in a follow-up. Protected TPU promotion requires a passing runtime gate, so this pair cannot be promoted before that follow-up fixes the import. The [normal physical qualification workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/actions/runs/38084197077) reached its 80-minute workflow limit while waiting for v6e-4 in `marin/europe-west4` at interactive priority. No worker was assigned and no execution attempt occurred. Workflow cleanup succeeded and the Iris job is terminal. Physical runtime validation remains unexecuted. The workflow now requests 64 GiB of disk; its former 100 GiB request exceeded the 90.6 GB reported by registered v6e-4 workers.

Keep this draft pending the normal hardware gate and protected promotion. Rollback sources are vLLM `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3` and tpu-inference `a8fc5c9f6d14ac5a3b1f97d5c296d6015a73cabe`. The [admin promotion handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10022#issuecomment-6093743002) records the remaining release gates, source promotion order and rollback refs.

topics.title: [levanter] Bound in-flight W&B metric host copies
topics.body:
Keep at most 8 device-to-host copies ahead of the value being read when converting a W&B payload. #9600 started a copy for every array leaf at once.

PJRT's GPU client finishes pending copies on a work queue (`pjrt_async_work_runner`) that starts a thread whenever queued work exceeds its idle threads and never stops one. A step's outputs become ready together, so prefetching a watch-step payload released thousands of copies at once and grew the queue by hundreds of threads in every process. The threads inherit the name `py_xla_callback` because their own name exceeds Linux's 15-character limit. On a one-rack restore of the hero run, each training process grew from 1 to about 1,700 `py_xla_callback` threads within 20 minutes, about 3,400 threads in total. Each blocking py-spy dump pauses every thread, so dumps took about 3.5x longer; #9998 makes Iris's periodic dumps non-blocking.

A single-node GB200 repro (4 processes, d768 MoE, watch every 10 steps) puts the growth at #9600: its parent and main with #9600 reverted keep 1 `py_xla_callback` thread per process, and #9600 has 318–424. With 2,000 scalars converted by `_convert_metrics_to_wandb_loggable` on one GPU:

| | `py_xla_callback` threads | conversion time |
|---|---|---|
| before #9600 | 1 | 60 ms |
| #9600 | 418 | 31 ms |
| this change | 2 | 33 ms |

topics.title: Plateau Dropping: per-token loss-plateau gating for agentic SFT
topics.body: # Plateau Dropping: per-token loss-plateau gating for agentic SFT **Summary.** Track every token's SFT loss across epochs and stop the gradient from tokens whose loss has plateaued; let them re-enter if their loss moves again. On the Grug 09.21 base and the run7 agentic mix this gives +4 pp pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2 and +5 pp on TB-Lite over plain SFT, holds the gain through pass@4, and matches plain SFT at pass@8. A random-drop control equals plain SFT and a confidence-only drop is worse than plain SFT, so the loss history is what matters. Preliminary SWE-bench Verified numbers after SFT on Open-SWE-Traces show a larger gap. ## Method - For each trained token position (document, offset) keep its loss at the last two visits and a visit count. - From a token's third visit on, if its last two visit-to-visit relative loss changes are both < 10 % (with a 0.05-nat floor on the denominator), its loss term is masked out of the batch loss. The token still goes through the forward pass and still sits in the context; only its gradient contribution is removed. If its loss moves again, it re-enters. - Everything else is plain SFT: same data, learning rate, window, batch, and schedule; the loss is averaged over kept tokens. - On the run7 mix about 65 % of tokens are dropped per batch once every token has three visits: ~60 % because they are learned (loss < 0.1 nats), ~5 % because they never move (example-specific paths, hashes). The all-token training loss stays within 0.005 nats of plain SFT. Loosely inspired by GRPO discarding all-correct and all-wrong groups: positions that carry no learning signal stop driving the update. TailSFT (trajectory-level) and turn-level variants of it did not move pass@k over plain SFT on these tasks. ## Setup - Base: Grug 67B-A2B 09.21. Data: run7 mix, 6,301 MiniSweAgent trajectories / 45.0M tokens / 1,610 tasks (5,324 allenai/tmax-sft successes from Qwen3.6-27B + 977 reward-1 rollouts of the base model on Endless Terminals + Recursive-Task-Synthesis). 32k window, lr 1e-4, one pass = 21.5 steps. - Arms: plain SFT 66 steps (3 ep, the run7 checkpoint), plain SFT 220 steps (10 ep, matched compute), plateau dropping 220 and 440 steps (10 and 20 ep), plus the base model. - Eval: all 89 TB2 and 100 TB-Lite tasks, MiniSweAgent harness, 3x task timeouts, temperature 1, one vLLM server per attempt, 8 attempts per task (base: 3). pass = reward 1; timeouts count as failures; trials that died on infrastructure errors are discarded. pass@k is the unbiased estimator; each panel uses every task with >= k valid attempts in all arms shown; error bars are SE over tasks. Every number was recounted independently and matches harbor's own job summaries. ## Results TB2 (88 / 88 / 88 / 74 matched tasks): | arm | pass@1 | pass@2 | pass@4 | pass@8 | |---|---|---|---|---| | base 09.21, no SFT | 8.5 | 13.3 | - | - | | plain SFT, 3 ep (66 steps) | 9.8 | 15.8 | 23.6 | 35.1 | | plain SFT, 10 ep (220 steps) | 11.8 | 17.4 | 23.4 | 31.1 | | plateau dropping, 10 ep (220 steps) | 11.7 | 18.7 | 26.1 | 33.8 | | plateau dropping, 20 ep (440 steps) | **14.1** | **20.4** | **26.7** | 31.1 | TB-Lite (98 / 98 / 98 / 90 matched tasks): | arm | pass@1 | pass@2 | pass@4 | pass@8 | |---|---|---|---|---| | plain SFT, 3 ep | 21.8 | 32.9 | 44.1 | 54.4 | | plain SFT, 10 ep | 21.4 | 32.0 | 43.0 | 55.6 | | plateau dropping, 10 ep | 24.1 | 35.3 | 47.4 | **60.0** | | plateau dropping, 20 ep | **26.6** | **38.8** | **49.6** | 57.8 | Paired against the 3-epoch plain checkpoint, the 20-epoch run is +4.2 +- 2.1 (TB2) and +4.8 +- 1.7 (TB-Lite) at pass@1. The gain narrows as k grows: at pass@8 the 10-epoch run holds it on TB-Lite (+5.6 +- 4.6) and is level on TB2; the 20-epoch run is level on TB-Lite and gives back a few points on TB2 (-4.1 +- 4.1). The rule makes the model solve the same tasks more reliably rather than solve new ones. Plain SFT at 10 epochs sharpens too but loses coverage (TB2 pass@8 -4.1). ## Ablations (220 steps, drop from step 65, 3 attempts, paired vs plain 3 ep) | arm | TB2 pass@1 | TB-Lite pass@1 | |---|---|---| | random 65 % of tokens dropped | +2.9 +- 2.8 (= plain SFT 10 ep) | -0.8 +- 3.2 | | confidence-only drop (p > 0.9, no history) | -1.9 +- 2.1 | **-11.5 +- 3.1** | | plateau dropping, 10 ep | +2.9 +- 2.9 | +4.1 +- 2.9 | | plateau dropping, 20 ep | +7.2 +- 2.7 | +4.5 +- 2.9 | | EMA variant of the plateau test, 20 ep | +7.2 +- 3.6 | -1.2 +- 3.1 | | plateau dropping, 40 ep | +6.3 +- 2.9 | +4.5 +- 3.4 | Random dropping = plain SFT; dropping by confidence alone hurts; 40 epochs adds nothing over 20; the EMA variant keeps the TB2 gain and loses the TB-Lite one. ## SWE-bench Verified (preliminary) Both arms SFT'd for 20 passes (1,520 steps, 64k window) on nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces v1.2 mini-swe-agent trajectories (Qwen3.8-27B thinking teacher, resolved, one bash call per turn, 9,229 trajectories / 319M tokens), evaluated under the same MiniSweAgent harness on a random 100 of SWE-bench Verified, 3 attempts. With ~40 % of trials in: plateau dropping ~38 % pass@1 vs ~17 % for plain SFT and ~17 % for the base; paired on common tasks +21 +- 5. Trajectory checks show both arms are format-healthy (< 2 % turns without a tool call). Final numbers to follow.

topics.title: [inference] Eval runner keeps a stale serve endpoint after the serve job is preempted
topics.body:
When an Iris serve job started by `marin.inference.iris.remote_inference` (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py`, `_start_direct_inference` / `_wait_for_endpoint`) is preempted by Kueue and its retry attempt registers a new endpoint on another host, the running evaluation keeps the first host:port it resolved. The Evalchemy chat client then loops on `ClientConnectorError` / `ReadTimeout` (or gets HTTP 404 from whatever now listens on that address) until the group's timeout or a manual cancel. The serve job itself is fine; only the client is stale.

Observed in marin #9920 and #9984 on cw-rno2a, 2026-10-09/10: nine evaluation groups lost this way (examples: `/karan/eval-20261009-030945-gate-rs-sft-lr1e-06-step375-5e80`, serve child `inference-553ee1e1…` preempted 6× and re-registered on 10.168.194.211 at 04:25 UTC while the eval kept 10.168.192.27:10241; `/karan/eval-20261010-030426-gate-merge-ta-a1.0-b1.0-gpqa28k-152a`, 188 logged requests answered 404 by the old address). Each costs the serve's partial GPU time plus a full relaunch; several evals ran 16–20 h before being noticed.

Expected: the client re-resolves the endpoint from the Iris registry when requests fail with connection errors (and periodically), and fails fast with a clear error when the serve job reaches a terminal state instead of retrying forever.

Done when: an eval whose serve is preempted and re-registered elsewhere continues against the new address, and an eval whose serve job dies fails within a bounded time with the serve job's state in the error.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Evalchemy launches with direct routing, and the orchestrator resolves the serve endpoint once before putting that pod address in the child job's config. The child keeps using that address while `eval_job.wait(timeout=inf)` blocks; serve health is checked only before and after the evaluation. [PR #9480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9480) chose direct routing after 7,734 hub and 10,749 peer proxy 502s in five minutes, so the recovery path must preserve direct connection reuse.

**Relevant code**
- [`launch.py#L195`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/experiments/evaluation/launch.py#L195) — selects direct Evalchemy routing
- [`runner.py#L352-L363`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L352-L363) — resolves before evaluation
- [`runner.py#L602-L609`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L602-L609) — turns registry entry into a fixed URL
- [`evalchemy/runner.py#L223-L233`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L223-L233) — serializes the URL into the child
- [`evalchemy/runner.py#L327`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L327) — waits without checking serve state

# Proposed Fix

1. Pass the endpoint name and serve job IDs to the Evalchemy child. Point Evalchemy at a loopback HTTP forwarder in that child; the forwarder uses a pooled connection to the current direct Iris endpoint and preserves streaming responses.
2. Refresh the registry address periodically and immediately after connection errors, timeouts, or a 404. Replace the upstream pool when the address changes, retry requests that have not started a response, and wait through a live job's preemption; propagate a 404 from an unchanged current address.
3. Poll serve status while the parent waits for the Evalchemy job. On a terminal serve state, cancel the evaluator and record `INFRA_FAILED` with the serve job ID and state within one poll interval; update both evaluation call paths to pass the inference session.
4. Cover address replacement, a stale-address 404, streaming interruption, recovery with no registered endpoint, and terminal serve state using local HTTP servers and a fake registry. Compare request failures and latency at Evalchemy's default concurrency before replacing direct routing.

topics.title: [rolloutengine] Reasoning-only truncation crashes grading preparation
topics.body:
A live Snowball → RolloutEngine smoke on TaskTrove UnitSyn returned `finish_reason="length"`, `content=null`, reasoning text, and no tool calls. RolloutEngine raised during grading: `ValueError: Chat response requires assistant content or function calls`. The task grader never ran.

Reproduce:
1. Return that message from the model adapter with valid token evidence for a graded task.
2. `_ShellboxTaskSession.advance` ends the turn with `invalid_assistant_message`.
3. `_grade_rollout` calls `chat_conversation` on the same message and raises before capturing files or invoking the grader.

Expected: preserve the truncated response and termination reason without crashing submission preparation. Keep usable prior answers/files available to the task grader; represent a missing answer explicitly so grading policy can decide its outcome. Do not gate all grading on `finish_reason="stop"`: file submissions can be valid when a turn/token limit ends an attempt.

Observed on merged #10029 (`7405c96fe6ea`). Relevant code: `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/{task_session,grading}.py` and `lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/chat.py`. Cover reasoning-only truncation and truncation after a usable file submission.

**Relevant code**
- [`task_session.py#L98-L105`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/task_session.py#L98-L105) - ends invalid assistant turns
- [`grading.py#L24-L47`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L24-L47) - parses before capturing files
- [`chat.py#L53-L70`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/chat.py#L53-L70) - rejects absent content and calls

# Proposed Fix

`run()` records the raw truncated message, `advance()` ends the turn, then `_grade_rollout()` passes that message to `chat_conversation()` and raises. Normalize a terminal assistant message with no content or calls to an empty assistant answer only in grading evidence; retain the raw message and `length` stop reason in the rollout record, then let the answer or file grader decide the result. topics.title: [iris] Follow re-registered serve endpoints from Evalchemy evals
topics.body:
Evalchemy children now reach their serve through a loopback relay that looks
the endpoint name up in the Iris registry, instead of a host:port resolved once
at launch. When Kueue preempts the serve and its retry registers on another
host, the old address refuses connections, hangs, or answers 404. The eval used
to retry that address until the group timed out: nine groups on cw-rno2a were
lost this way on 2026-10-09/10, some after 16-20 h.

The relay (iris.cluster.client.endpoint_relay) looks the name up every 30 s and
after each connection failure or 404. It aborts requests still waiting on a
replaced address and replays requests that have no response yet once the
endpoint is registered again (for up to 1 h, then 503). A response that has
started is never replayed; the relay drops the client connection so lm-eval's
own retries apply. Each relay thread keeps a pooled direct connection, so evals
keep the direct routing that #9480 chose over the hub proxy.

The fix sits in an Iris client module so any in-cluster client can use it. A
stable cluster-level address (a per-endpoint Kubernetes Service, or
controller-side forwarding) would cover every client without a helper process,
but it needs a controller deploy and work in each backend. The hub proxy
already follows re-registrations, and it is the path #9480 moved away from. The
relay ships in the job bundle and takes effect on the next eval launch.

While the Evalchemy job runs, the parent now reads the serve job states every
60 s. When one is terminal, it cancels the Evalchemy job and the record becomes
infra_failed with the serve job ID and state. A failed status read does not end
the eval. Before, the parent waited with no bound.

Tests drive the relay with real HTTP servers and a fake registry whose endpoint
moves mid-run. On a local in-process Iris cluster, the relay CLI in a client
task followed a serve job that was cancelled and replaced under the same
endpoint name; the request in flight during the gap waited about 4 s and was
answered by the replacement. Not yet run on CoreWeave: the registry lookup with
a task token (the local cluster has no auth) and starting the relay from
$IRIS_VENV inside a real Evalchemy child.

Fixes #10030

topics.title: [inference] Eval runner counts a Kueue-gated serve pod as placed and burns the startup budget while queued
topics.body:
`marin.inference.iris._wait_for_endpoint` (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py`) budgets serve startup with `ENDPOINT_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (2,400 s) only while a task is placed, and queue time separately with a 4 h placement budget. It decides placement with `_PLACED_TASK_STATES = {ASSIGNED, BUILDING, RUNNING}`. The Iris k8s backend (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py`, Pending branch) reports every Pending pod as `TASK_STATE_BUILDING`, including a pod that Kueue holds behind a scheduling gate (status message starts with `SchedulingGated: Scheduling is blocked due to non-empty scheduling gates; Kueue workload …`). So a serve that is merely queued is treated as starting, and the evaluation fails with `Timed out waiting for inference endpoint` after 40 minutes while no GPU was ever allocated.

Observed 2026-10-11 on cw-rno2a (marin #9984): eval groups `/karan/eval-20261010-231346-gate-mixed-rs-lr1e-06-step364-dda9`, `/karan/eval-20261011-000224-gate-mixed-rs-lr1e-06-step546-0e65`, `/karan/eval-20261011-005242-gate-mixed-rs-lr1e-06-step727-b634` (and five more the same night): each serve child ended `killed` with task duration `-`, preemptions 0 and the SchedulingGated diagnostic; each eval task ran 40 min and recorded infra_failed.

Expected: a gated pod counts as queued (placement budget), and the startup budget starts only when the pod is scheduled (node assigned / container started). Done when: a serve held in a Kueue gate for longer than the startup budget still produces a successful evaluation once admitted, and a unit test covers gated → placed → requeued timing of the two budgets.

🤖 # Research

`_wait_for_endpoint()` treats every `BUILDING` task as placed. The Kubernetes backend reports a Pending pod as `BUILDING` before Kueue removes its scheduling gate, so the 2,400-second startup deadline can expire without a node assignment. No open PR overlaps this fix.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris.py#L539-L579`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py#L539-L579) - placement and deadline logic
- [`tasks.py#L1251-L1266`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L1251-L1266) - Pending pod state and node identity
- [`workload.py#L91-L127`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/client/workload.py#L91-L127) - exposed worker and node fields

# Proposed Fix

Kueue-gated Pending pod → `BUILDING` task → `_PLACED_TASK_STATES` → startup timeout. Count a task as placed only when its current attempt has a node, its Iris worker is assigned, or it is running; keep requeued tasks on the placement budget. Add a waiter regression test for gated → placed → requeued → admitted timing.

🤖 PR #10038 starts the 2,400-second startup budget only after the current attempt has a worker or node assignment, or the task runs; it ignores federated peer display labels while gated pods remain on the four-hour placement budget. A regression covers gating, placement, requeue, and readmission; 95 evaluation tests and PR CI pass. Incident record: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/700. The PR is open and mergeable, awaiting review after the 12-hour monitor timed out.

topics.title: [marin] Keep Kueue-gated serve tasks in the placement budget
topics.body:
Iris reports a Pending pod as BUILDING, including a pod that Kueue still holds at its admission gate (status message `SchedulingGated: ...`). The eval runner's endpoint wait in `marin.inference.iris` counted BUILDING as placed, so the 2,400 s startup budget ran while the serve job was still queued for GPUs. Eight eval groups failed this way in one night with no GPU allocated.

A BUILDING task whose status message starts with `SchedulingGated` now counts as queued. The 4 h placement budget covers gated time, and the startup budget starts only once the gate is lifted. A preemption requeue still resets the startup budget. The wait now reads per-task status with `list_tasks` because the job-level state counts do not carry the status message.

A pod that Kueue has admitted but the scheduler reports `Unschedulable` still counts as placed, so the startup budget bounds an admitted pod that does not start. `Unschedulable` can mean a bad resource request or ordinary capacity or affinity limits; this keeps the existing behavior for both.

Separate from #10030 / #10033.

Fixes #10036

topics.title: [inference] Start serve readiness timeout after placement
topics.body:
Start the serve readiness timeout when a task's current attempt has an assigned Iris worker or a node-bound Kubernetes pod, or when the task is running. Kubernetes reports Kueue-gated Pending pods as BUILDING; the previous state-count check treated them as placed and failed evaluations after 2,400 seconds without allocating a GPU. Federated task status can also show a peer display label as its worker ID before placement, so the waiter uses the current attempt's assignment.

Queued time remains subject to the four-hour placement deadline. Requeued attempts stop consuming the startup budget, and old attempts' placement details do not mark the new attempt as placed.

Fixes #10036

topics.title: [levanter] Exclude cache markers from Hugging Face mirrors
topics.body:
Skip a Hugging Face repository file when its name matches the configured cache completion marker. The DARE-TIES-02 repository contains `.cache_metadata.json` from its Base cache. During streaming, that file reached the regional mirror before all weight shards. A follower then logged a cache hit on a 90 GB mirror containing only 28 of 39 shards.

The regression test interrupts a weight download and verifies that the marker remains absent until a successful retry. Existing partial mirrors with a copied marker need separate cleanup.

topics.title: [experiment] BFCL multi-harness DPO recovery: results and remaining work
topics.body:
## TL;DR

The BFCL multi-harness recovery campaign did not reach its goal. We exercised DPO (direct preference optimization) in Levanter, implemented and tested native DPO in MarinSkyRL, and built trace retention, preference curation, and multi-harness collection infrastructure. The extended native DPO run degraded Pi accuracy from 34/123 at initialization to 10/123 after four updates and 0/123 after eight; we stopped it after preserving intermediate evaluations. Harness transfer was partial and large score differences persisted across harnesses. A separate model-merging campaign recovered substantially more measured BFCL-Parity performance than the DPO recipes tested here, with important selection and comparability limits.

## Description

The original objective was to improve function calling from the Grug-67B-A2B Antidoom/RLVR1 step-12 lineage and demonstrate multi-harness robustness: the worst harness should reach at least 70% of the best harness's score. Grug is a mixture-of-experts model with approximately 67 billion total and 2 billion active parameters; Antidoom/RLVR1 identifies its prior de-looping and reinforcement-learning checkpoint lineage. Labels such as `.304` and `.356` are campaign run/artifact identifiers. Training used the 3,518-task BFCL complement, excluding the 123 BFCL-Parity tasks. Offline DPO was used to improve the weak starting policy before attempting further online RL.

BFCL-Parity is Harbor's `bfcl_parity@1.0` adaptation of the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard. Pi, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Mini-SWE are agent harnesses that provide prompts, tool interfaces, and execution loops around the model. Each evaluation task receives one agent trial; accuracy means passing the task verifier. These tasks require `/app/result.json`, whose existence alone is insufficient for success. The scores below are adaptation-specific solve rates, not standard BFCL leaderboard scores. See the [public evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9566).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Learn function-calling behavior that transfers across harnesses while preserving task accuracy. The campaign tested whole-trajectory preference training, not the localized token/action objectives proposed in the follow-ups.

## Status

Learning work is stopped. The campaign achieved these infrastructure milestones:

- Levanter DPO produced the `.304` initializer after two additional optimizer updates and a 39-shard HF-format export. This checkpoint descended from an earlier 58-update DPO warm start; it was not trained directly from the original model in two updates. [Export receipt](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/daytona-expanded-training-v304-verified.json).
- Native DPO was [merged into MarinSkyRL in #954](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/954). Pipeline smoke `.356` connected fresh collection, curation, four applied updates, Pi evaluation, and export. Its 64-pair batch contained one newly collected pair; this was not an all-harness fresh-data smoke. Accuracy fell from 28/123 to 7/123. [Optimizer and pipeline receipt](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/final-pipeline-v356-verified.json).
- The collection/curation path retains teacher/student traces, exact tokens and masks where captured, verifier outcomes, task identities, immutable partial batches, and preference provenance. Four harnesses supplied the final training cohort; Pi was the evaluation harness. These components support future datakit mining, but do not yet implement verified same-history local repair pairs. [Infrastructure inventory](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/technical-progress-20261011.md), [pinned campaign code](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl).
- A complete online multi-harness RL optimizer loop was not demonstrated. Collection, native trace capture, rollout configuration, and training components exist; their full on-policy integration remains unverified. Some fixes remain on campaign branches or open PRs.

The final native DPO input contained 1,712 pairs from 633 tasks unseen by the initializer's recorded training lineage. We planned 107 updates at 16 pairs/update, with Pi validation before training and every four updates. Applied updates are verified through 35, with nine completed evaluation panels and a partial update-36 panel. The initializer remained the best evaluated checkpoint. [Collapse analysis](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/dpo-collapse-investigation-20261011.md), [archive/stop receipt](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/final-dpo-forensics-stop-verified.json).

## Results and limits

Levanter's short `.304` continuation improved the measured panel relative to its `.26` warm start: Pi 23/122 to 35/123, Claude Code 15/123 to 29/123, OpenCode 8/123 to 24/123, and Mini-SWE 8/123 to 16/123. The Pi baseline attempted 123 tasks with one infrastructure-ungraded result. These are single panel comparisons, not repeated statistical estimates. Public warm-start receipts: [Pi](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-pi-verified.json), [Claude Code](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-claude-code-verified.json), [OpenCode](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-opencode-verified.json), [Mini-SWE](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-mini-swe-agent-verified.json).

The earlier `.304` panel scored Pi 35/123 (28.46%), Claude Code 29/123 (23.58%), OpenCode 24/123 (19.51%), and Mini-SWE 16/123 (13.01%). Codex covered only 105/123 tasks and was not a valid canonical panel. The worst valid score was 46% of the best, below the required 70%. These results show harness-dependent performance; they do not isolate a causal training-mixture effect. The later 34/123 native-run baseline is a separate evaluation of the initializer.

The best related published merge, [Shared100](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-NUPA-BFCL-Shared100-2026.10.09/tree/462ad9af071055da39ef4bfea1d4ba2c9429a223), scored 60/123 (48.78%) on BFCL-Parity Pi, versus `.304`'s 35/123. In our experiments, merging recovered more measured performance than the tested DPO recipes. However, BFCL-Parity activation traces informed expert selection in the merge campaign, and the benchmark was reused for model selection. Its score is an optimization result, not a clean held-out or controlled causal comparison with DPO. Parent mixtures and training histories differ, and the merge's Pi score does not establish multi-harness robustness. [Merge campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9975).

At native DPO update 8, all 123 tasks lacked the required result file. Successful file-writing demonstrations existed in the preference data. Rejected responses contributed about 7.24 times as many supervised tokens as chosen responses, with extreme tool-syntax repetition. These observations motivate local, bounded training targets. They do not establish the precise gradient mechanism behind the collapse. Independent distributed-update and training-to-serving numerical equivalence remain [deferred verification experiments](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/969), not discovered bugs.

## Links

Datakit is [Marin's data preparation and chat-rendering library](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit). Linked historical reports retain local/internal provenance paths; the public release supports aggregate inspection rather than complete independent replay. Evaluation runtime pins also differ between the DPO and merge campaigns, so their results are separate campaign measurements.

- [Public screened campaign artifacts](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/tree/9be5d36578c27140a75caac1e31ecdefb76cff0b): 7,356 files, reports, scripts, configurations, aggregate receipts, model publication verification, and an exclusion manifest. Raw conversations, private DPO datasets, third-party payloads, secrets, and runtime directories are withheld. Public aggregates do not permit independent replay of every private-trace analysis.
- [Best DPO initializer, BFCL-Recovery (`.304`)](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-BFCL-Recovery/tree/850a32627724d274004241dd10f6cb46fd3f6f83): public, 39 BF16 shards, with all uploaded file hashes verified. The model card explains the inherited stale manifest and the scope of provenance checks. It received no updates from the degrading extended run. [Best related published merge and limitations](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-NUPA-BFCL-Shared100-2026.10.09/tree/462ad9af071055da39ef4bfea1d4ba2c9429a223) is a separate model.
- [Pinned MarinSkyRL runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/fa6da4d8c67ed17b3fa69f689d9b444694683f8a), [pinned Harbor runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/436d0c92ed2fbb679438cd750e5fab3328153c31).
- Open follow-ups: [localized online feedback #10043](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043), [datakit single-turn comparison mining and DPO validation #10042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10042), and [complete online multi-harness RL integration #10041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10041).

## Decision Log

- Used offline preference learning while baseline task success remained low.
- Moved from Levanter to native MarinSkyRL DPO to exercise the unified trainer and periodic Pi evaluation.
- Stopped the extended run after degradation, preserving intermediate traces for analysis.
- Separated future behavioral interventions from the uncompleted online integration work.

## Conclusion

The performance and harness-robustness objectives remain unmet. The campaign leaves tested DPO plumbing and reusable collection/curation components, with three explicit follow-ups. Closing this issue archives the campaign; it does not certify successful recovery or complete online multi-harness RL.

topics.title: Complete and validate online multi-harness RL integration
topics.body:
Complete the integration and end-to-end validation of online multi-harness RL in MarinSkyRL through Marin's BFCL entrypoint. The campaign demonstrated multi-harness collection and native offline DPO, but did not verify a complete online RL optimizer update. Most underlying components exist; this task should connect and validate them rather than introduce a parallel training stack.

The [public readiness inventory](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/technical-progress-20261011.md) identifies the concrete gap: the older online launcher has four harness profiles and an RL recipe, but disables inline evaluation and resolves an older recovery export. The native DPO path has the demonstrated Pi evaluation and checkpoint/export wiring. [Pinned Marin entrypoints](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl), [MarinSkyRL runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/fa6da4d8c67ed17b3fa69f689d9b444694683f8a), [Harbor runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/436d0c92ed2fbb679438cd750e5fab3328153c31).

Done when:

- Wire an explicitly pinned initializer, current Daytona backend/snapshot handling, live policy inference, harness assignment, native trace/token/logprob capture, reward/advantage construction, optimizer updates, inference synchronization, and recurring evaluation into one maintained entrypoint.
- Make harness assignment and mixture weights explicit. Existing task-index routing does not establish randomized same-task cross-harness coverage. Preserve native tool interfaces and exact model-visible history, including multi-turn compaction and generation masks.
- Demonstrate single-harness smokes for Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, and Mini-SWE, then a mixed-harness smoke. Require actual non-skipped optimizer updates and subsequent rollouts from updated weights, finite training metrics, correct policy-version provenance, save/resume, and an independently loadable export. Successful job exit alone is insufficient.
- Verify reward/error taxonomy: infrastructure failures are not silently treated as policy failures, and policy-scoreable errors retain verifier outcomes. Exercise timeouts, missing tool results, and partial completed batches without discarding valid immutable work.
- Connect baseline, periodic, and terminal Pi validation using the demonstrated native evaluation path; run separate full panels across harnesses for cross-harness assessment. A single inline harness does not establish multi-harness robustness.
- Run a bounded online learning experiment on complement-only tasks, with no BFCL-Parity training leakage. Publish exact pins, placement, hyperparameters, update/rollout receipts, costs, and policy-matched results. Separately report integration completion and whether task performance improves.
- Record the original campaign's unresolved scientific target: substantial BFCL-Parity improvement with the worst harness at least 70% of the best. Failure to achieve that target must not erase a verified integration result, nor should an integration pass be called learning success.

The [native DPO smoke](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/final-pipeline-v356-verified.json) provides a reuse target, not evidence that online RL is complete. [Distributed numerical-equivalence experiments](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/969) remain a separate verification follow-up, not three established defects or a prerequisite for this integration task. [Campaign closeout #10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040); related work: [localized online feedback #10043](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043) and [datakit local-pair mining #10042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10042).

topics.title: Mine and validate same-history local DPO pairs with datakit
topics.body:
Design, implement, execute, and validate reusable datakit tooling that turns retained agent traces into same-history, single-turn preference examples, then determine whether DPO learns the intended local behavior without degrading task performance. The BFCL campaign already retains traces, preference provenance, task identities, and token masks; verified local-pair extraction remains to be built. [Infrastructure inventory](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/technical-progress-20261011.md).

A bounded bad action is one erroneous tool action or a precisely identified invalid token transition, excluding an arbitrarily long rejected continuation. A verified repair is a replacement supported by explicit protocol, execution, or task-level checks. The preferred and rejected action must share exactly the same conditioning history and tool schema; counterfactual execution also requires equivalent environment state. A later successful retry is not automatically a valid pair because its history contains additional observations.

Datakit is [Marin's data preparation and chat-rendering library](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit); DPO means direct preference optimization. Linked historical reports contain internal provenance paths and withheld-input references; they support public aggregate inspection, not complete independent replay.

Successful calls from otherwise unsuccessful trials are eligible positive examples. Record their evidence level: parser/schema validity, execution success, or task-verifier success. Do not equate these levels or put future tool results into the model's conditioning history.

Done when:

- Audit the existing training-complement corpus and publish eligible counts by harness, task, failure class, and evidence level. Report losses from missing exact histories or unreplayable state; do not presume a large usable yield.
- Implement deterministic extraction for unambiguous repairs and controlled corruptions of verified valid actions. Treat retry mining as a candidate source requiring prefix/state checks. Preserve originals, task/trajectory IDs, hashes, policy/harness versions, repair rules, and verification receipts.
- Emit standard preference artifacts with exact token histories and explicit supervised spans. Bound negative-action length, cap contributions per trajectory/task, deduplicate, and exclude holdout tasks and previously trained task identities as required by the experiment. Validate masks through the production renderer.
- Add behavior-focused tests for identical-prefix enforcement, task leakage, synthetic corruption validity, token-boundary preservation, and mask placement. Distinguish observed negatives from synthetic ones.
- Execute small controlled native DPO runs comparing the extracted local pairs with filtered whole-trace pairs and positive-only masked SFT. Explicitly configure beta, learning rate, sequence/token normalization, masks, batch composition, and reference initialization; vary one factor at a time where possible.
- Demonstrate actual updates and evaluate targeted validity/execution, task success, and cross-harness effects. Publish negative results and a reusable recipe even if DPO does not outperform the simpler control.
- Keep source datasets private unless independently cleared for redistribution; release tooling and aggregate evidence without proprietary harness scaffolding.

[Public collapse analysis](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/dpo-collapse-investigation-20261011.md) documents the rejected-loop imbalance motivating bounded examples. It does not prove that this change will repair the model. [Campaign closeout #10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040); related work: [localized online feedback #10043](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043) and [online multi-harness integration #10041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10041).

# Research

The pinned BFCL pipeline retains per-step prompt tokens, response tokens, and loss masks, but its existing preference artifact contains whole trajectories. Pair selection checks the initial prompt and verifier outcome; it does not establish identical conditioning history or environment state at a later tool action. The stopped run's 1,712 pairs came from 633 tasks, and rejected branches had 7.24 times as many supervised tokens as chosen branches ([campaign analysis](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/dpo-collapse-investigation-20261011.md)); the public archive cannot establish a usable local-pair count because raw traces are withheld.

**Relevant code**
- [`retained_preferences.py#L115-L149`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/retained_preferences.py#L115-L149) — exact step tokens and boundaries
- [`retained_preferences.py#L197-L214`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/retained_preferences.py#L197-L214) — whole-trajectory pair encoding
- [`offline_preferences.py#L353-L401`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/offline_preferences.py#L353-L401) — initial-context check and cache
- [`data.py#L19-L69`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/data.py#L19-L69) — pinned task identities and holdout
- [`final_dpo.py#L117-L174`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/final_dpo.py#L117-L174) — native DPO input and recipe

# Proposed design

## Goal and constraint

Produce auditable single-action preference rows and test whether they improve tool behavior without reducing BFCL task success. The first deliverable is a yield audit, since the released aggregates do not show how many private traces have both an exact action prefix and replayable state. Keep source traces and task payloads private; publish tooling, counts, rejection reasons, and screened receipts.

## Plan

1. **Audit the frozen training complement.** Pin collection manifests, task digests, policy and harness revisions, renderer/tokenizer, and initializer training lineage. Stream retained records and native trace/verification receipts without copying bulk source data. Count candidate actions by harness, task, failure class, and evidence level (parser/schema, execution, task verifier); count exclusions for missing exact history, unknown pre-action state, absent receipt, overlength action, duplicate, holdout, and previously trained task ID. A successful call within a failed trial can supply a positive action when its own receipt supports that level of claim. Publish the census before selecting a training recipe.

2. **Add a deterministic datakit extractor and a versioned artifact contract.** Each row carries one exact prompt-token prefix, tool-schema hash, chosen/rejected action token IDs and supervised spans, task/trajectory IDs, source hashes and URIs, policy/harness versions, pre-action state evidence, repair rule/version, verification receipts, evidence level, and whether the negative was observed or synthetic. Form an observed pair only when the token prefix, tool schema, and pre-action state match; a later retry is only a candidate. Generate synthetic negatives by one seeded, bounded corruption of a verified valid action, then check the intended failure with the relevant parser, executor, or task verifier. Reject ambiguous repairs and unverifiable state-dependent comparisons.

3. **Filter and validate before training.** Exclude parity and initializer-trained task identities, deduplicate by task plus prefix and action hashes, and deterministically cap contributions per task and trajectory. Start with a 512-token action limit, four pairs per task, and one pair per trajectory; report the yield under these caps and at 256/1024 tokens before freezing them. Emit the native `chosen_input_ids`/`rejected_input_ids` and assistant-mask columns with identical prefix IDs and zero supervision outside the two action spans. Check token boundaries and masks against the production chat renderer; reject any row whose rendered history differs from the retained prefix. Test prefix/state mismatch, leakage, observed versus synthetic provenance, corruption verdicts, token boundaries, and mask placement using real fixtures.

4. **Run a bounded comparison only if the audit yields enough verified rows.** Freeze one task-disjoint local-pair artifact and matched controls: filtered whole-trajectory DPO and positive-only masked SFT. Use the same initializer, task exposure, evaluation runtime, and policy sampling. Record beta, learning rate, reference initialization, sequence/token normalization, masks, and pair composition explicitly; use the prior beta 0.1 and LR 4e-6 as a documented starting configuration, then change one factor at a time. Verify applied optimizer updates, evaluate action validity/execution and Pi task success at initialization and every four updates, then run complete cross-harness panels for promising checkpoints. Stop a pilot when task success or recognized tool execution collapses, and publish negative results as well as a reusable extraction and training recipe.

## Risks and open questions

Exact token history may be present while equivalent pre-action environment state is not; that reduces observed-pair yield and may leave only synthetic or parser-level examples. The audit should resolve whether retained state fingerprints or replay receipts can support execution-level pairing and whether the proposed contribution caps leave enough task-diverse examples for a meaningful pilot. Do not promote parser-valid actions to task-success labels or infer a win from a small validity improvement without task and cross-harness results.
