topics.title: [experiment] Snowball SFT on GLM-5.3 traces from Skill2Env biology tasks
topics.body:
## TL;DR

**Experiment finished on October 9, 2026.** Closing with no demonstrated improvement on the primary Pi/BixBench evaluation. The remaining uncertainties are recorded as limitations; no further training, evaluation, or investigation is planned under this issue.

The biology-only SFT run is complete, but the primary evaluation on **Pi**, the harness used to collect the teacher traces and intended for deployment, has not demonstrated improved BixBench performance. On five questions selected using historical runtime, **Pi with thinking enabled scored parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5**, with all attempts graded. The final response contained an unexecuted tool call in the parsed reasoning field in 1/5 parent attempts and 5/5 SFT attempts. The affected parent attempt had already written the correct answer and still received credit. Two SFT attempts executed no tools, while three executed tools before that ending. This failure therefore also exists in the parent; it was observed more often after SFT in this small sample. With thinking disabled, the parent scored 1/5; SFT had one correct and one incorrect graded attempt plus three verifier timeouts. Those missing grades prevent a complete accuracy comparison and are not counted as zero. This is a small diagnostic sample, not a full BixBench result. See the [primary Pi results and matched controls](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069563534).

The run used the September 21 Datakit parent, biology traces only, three epochs, peak LR 1e-4, 128k sequences, effective batch 16, and a final-only checkpoint. The dataset contains 5,120 reconstructed windows and 73,894,261 assistant target tokens per epoch from 1,319 attempts across 264 tasks, without reward/completion filtering or replay data. The [published-input audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069710545) found no supervised tool tags inside open reasoning; the cause of the observed Pi behavior remains unresolved.

Terminus-2 and the synthetic tasks are **secondary diagnostics** of format adherence and transfer to other harnesses. Terminus scored parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5 on the same real questions; this is not the primary measure of the Pi-trained model. The [Terminus trace analysis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083049902) and [completed prompt ablation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083809697) investigate format sensitivity. The latter accepted 36/36 parent versus 0/36 SFT first responses under the Terminus schema; this remains a secondary format-transfer diagnostic. A Terminus-specific workaround would not establish a fix for Pi.

## Description

Use the existing [Skill2Env Harbor release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env) to collect GLM-5.3 demonstrations for Snowball. This issue owns task selection, rollout collection, SFT, and the before/after experiment. [#9630](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9630) owns Skill2Env Atlas intake; [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258) owns biology evaluation coverage and protocols.

Start with biology tasks, prioritizing biological data analysis relevant to BixBench. If the usable pool is too small, consider a separately recorded expansion to general scientific data analysis and statistics. Keep relay methods, where a teacher takes over from student-generated actions, for a later experiment.

### Candidate data

The October 5 metadata inspection covered all 7,496 tasks in release revision 2, version `1.0.1`, with content digest `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. The 268 candidates are a source-skill and description-based shortlist, not an exhaustive taxonomy or a validated training pool.

| Candidate category | Tasks | Source-skill identifiers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Genomics and single-cell analysis | 95 | 40 |
| Proteins and structure | 49 | 16 |
| Chemistry and drug discovery | 45 | 22 |
| Biomedical data and lab workflows | 79 | 28 |
| Total | 268 | 106 |

Examples include paired airway RNA-seq analysis with PyDESeq2, sparse CELLxGENE summaries, Scanpy PBMC QC and clustering, DepMap dependency analysis, and pysam BAM/VCF processing. Different skill identifiers can cover related workflows; 106 identifiers do not establish 106 independent task families. Many released tasks repair pipelines against offline fixtures. Their usefulness for BixBench remains a hypothesis.

Skill2Env's [source attribution table](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env/blob/507eab4d9952968de2be98f8729d3c66d487285a/SkillHub/skillhub_source_licenses.csv) includes K-Dense scientific skills and AlterLab academic skills. Preserve task-specific source and license records when selecting data or sharing traces. The selection rule below preserves this initial shortlist independently of temporary local files.

### Pilot sequence

1. Review candidate instructions, environments, and graders. Six initial tasks passed reference/no-op controls. The user authorized direct collection on the other 262 metadata-selected candidates; those tasks have not passed additional controls. Review grader validity when interpreting scores; it is not a selection gate for the unfiltered baseline. Record any grader defects; the existing Atlas assessment found a grader defect in a separate three-task sample.
2. Freeze the task manifest and evaluation split. Group related tasks and shared-data variants when defining development and held-out sets. BixBench-overlap checking is not a prerequisite for this collection, as decided on October 5; preserve task provenance.
3. Pin the Snowball starting checkpoint, tokenizer, training recipe, agent harness, and evaluation settings. Run a small end-to-end collection and formatting check before expanding collection. Record compute budgets before launching sandbox or training work.
4. Generate GLM-5.3 trajectories. The initial collection finished five attempts per task on the six control-checked tasks, for 30 attempted rollouts. The expanded collection targets five attempts for each of the other 262 tasks, for 1,310 new attempts. Preserve every attempt, raw conversations, tool outputs, exact model settings, task revisions, and the full native reward vector; keep incomplete and ungraded outcomes separate. Inspect component-score distributions, solution diversity, and token volume. The first SFT baseline uses all available solver traces without reward or completion filtering. Preserve interrupted prefixes and record conversion or recovery gaps without manufacturing missing content. Rewards are graded; do not reduce them to binary success or require all components to equal 1 by default. Native executable rewards do not reproduce the paper's additional rubric-scoring layer.
5. Prepare all available solver traces for the first SFT baseline; the earlier 200–500 selected-trace target is superseded. Report attempted, complete, graded, and selected traces; component-score distributions; unique tasks and task families; total tokens; and supervised assistant tokens. Size the first SFT run from those observations; the target is a planning budget, not a proven minimum. Prioritize coverage of distinct tasks when expanding collection. Additional attempts on one task do not increase task diversity.
6. Train with loss on assistant turns, preserving user and tool messages as context. Evaluate the final checkpoint against the unchanged Snowball parent on the fixed BixBench protocol using the same Pi harness and budgets. Decide on broader evaluations after reviewing BixBench. Keep infrastructure failures separate from incorrect answers.

Recent Snowball work motivates a bounded test: a [5,000-conversation GLM continuation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9719) regressed on several benchmarks, while [other agent SFT mixtures](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/8669f5b6f97e4e3bae72344a8fd51f4b) improved agent benchmarks. Neither establishes a BixBench benefit from this dataset.

### Agreed SFT settings

| Setting | Selected value |
| --- | --- |
| Parent | `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`; revision `b8c07f7df1df65525abbfdbcd1572318ba11c42f` and native tokenizer/template pinned |
| Data | All available GLM/Pi biology solver traces; no reward or completion filter; no general SFT or pretraining replay |
| Run count and peak LR | One run at `1e-4` |
| Duration | Three epochs |
| Training sequence length | 131,072 tokens; verify actual lengths with the parent tokenizer |
| Effective global batch | 16 sequences per optimizer update; accumulation as needed |
| Parameter updates | Full-parameter SFT; imported router biases frozen, router weights and other model weights trained |
| Optimizer | Fresh AdamH; beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95, epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0, gradient clipping 1.0 |
| Schedule | 3% warmup, then cosine decay from 1e-4 to 1e-5 over the run |
| Checkpoints | Final model save/export only; no intermediate or per-epoch checkpoints |
| Initial evaluation | Parent and final model on BixBench with identical Pi harness and budgets; broader evaluations deferred until that result |

The nominal batch is 2,097,152 token positions per update, matching 64 × 32,768 in [the teacher-only reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9582). Masking, padding, and sequence construction determine actual supervised tokens. Three epochs and peak LR 1e-4 follow that precedent; its reported evaluations use final checkpoints, and its intermediate checkpoint cadence is undocumented. The final-only saving decision avoids repeated serialization and storage of this model.

Use reconstructed conversations with each actual assistant output supervised once, carried context masked, and interrupted outputs left without invented termination markers. The finalized dataset has 5,120 windows at length 131,072, 320 steps per epoch, and 960 steps total. Target four CoreWeave nodes with eight H100s each. BixBench comparison uses `bixbench-cli-marin-corrections@3` (205 tasks), Pi, one attempt per task, 32,768 context / 8,192 output, and matched grading. The CPU training coordinator is submitted; GPU training remains gated on cache verification.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Unfiltered GLM-5.3 demonstrations of biological analysis improve Snowball's held-out BixBench accuracy under the same harness and execution budget. Measure paired BixBench changes and uncertainty, task coverage, tool-format failures, and response lengths. Broader evaluation is deferred until the BixBench result. Review trace completeness, native grades, and sequence handling before training; preserve negative results.

## Status

The expanded collection completed all 1,310 original task/repetition slots. The final audit proves exactly five attempts per task, with no missing or duplicate pairs. Native reward vectors exist for 1,285 attempts; 25 are ungraded. There are 946 final assistant `stop` markers, 248 output-limit endings, 49 final tool-use stops, eight final error stops, and 59 without an exported final assistant stop reason. Agent timeouts are an overlapping exception class: 86 attempts record one. No verifier-error diagnostic was recorded. Native Pi sessions and ATIF trajectories are present for 1,251 attempts.

Native score patterns across the graded attempts are 574 vectors with every component equal to 1, 381 with mixed or partial component credit, and 330 with every component equal to 0. These remain graded vectors, not binary success labels. The 946 final `stop` markers cover 238 tasks; nine also record runner exceptions, so this marker alone does not establish a clean run. A historical structural screen requiring native session and trajectory, no exception or recorded verifier error, and matched tool calls/replies retains 933 normal candidates. Of those, 558 have every component equal to 1 and cover 161 tasks. Their provider-counted output usage totals 24,112,468 tokens; this includes reasoning and possible auxiliary compaction output and is not a unique Snowball-supervised token count. Four normal traces have unresolved tool-call diagnostics. These screening counts are diagnostic subsets and do not define the unfiltered training pool.

The original batch retained 875 attempts: 829 verified per-attempt archives and 46 [verified fallback recoveries](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6016912375). The continuation executed only the remaining 435 slots and verified all 435 checkpoints, with no further checkpoint failures. It completed at 14:46:11 UTC; cleanup at 14:46:14 reported zero owned sandboxes. The small final Iris archive and completion audit were copied to private durable storage and retrieved for SHA-256 verification. Final archive SHA-256: `4b06bdb9e491145acaddddb0cd44928191386b22b80b3061a3b1a18c5511e68a` (2,240,445 bytes). Original native grades, checkpoint-failure labels, and interrupted-stream diagnostics are preserved.

Both cohorts used native Pi 0.87.0 with 131,072 total context, 32,768 solver output, thinking enabled, native compaction, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, repetition seeds 0–4, and up to 64 concurrent workers. The continuation repaired capture closure and retried a startup that was preempted before teacher generation; it did not rerun attempted slots. Original expanded protocol SHA-256: `24ebb14feb54c3ec97f4c79732a7d42efb2c8cc7c792c2bc6e714dbeb6833997`; continuation: `36e7a611fb25f8e6625934b123ad00f6b33cdace57945b32d7ac5a7ef9852a58`; 262-task manifest: `87f0276f2fe2a3675eb875079363d20d321a80ca216e265539c39a6524f7cd75`. Source archives, notices, launch snapshots, native results, and raw captures are retained.

The six-task control batch is complete: all reference reward components were 1.0 and all no-op components were 0.0, with verifier diagnostics reviewed. The other candidates remain a metadata shortlist. The [seven-attempt Terminus-2 batch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6004311716) is retained separately as diagnostic evidence; its continuation is superseded.

Pi collection completed all 30 planned attempts and retained 29 native reward vectors. Endings: 17 normal, eight output-limited, four agent timeouts, and one ungraded `DaytonaBadGatewayError`. No verifier errors were recorded. The 17 normal traces have matched tool calls and replies, with full or partial native component credit. They cover DepMap, pysam, CELLxGENE, PyDESeq2, and Scanpy; all five scikit-bio attempts ended at an output limit. They contain 869,472 provider-counted output tokens before reward selection and target-tokenizer accounting. No filtering has been applied; the first baseline retains all available solver traces.

Native Pi sessions and ATIF trajectories were retained for 26/30 attempts. Three timeouts lost native log export because `pi.txt` changed during archiving; the infrastructure failure also lacks native agent logs. Raw API captures are retained for all 30 attempts, including three interrupted response streams. The four timeout traces contain repeated identical tool exchanges. The complete archive, source notices, per-file hashes, configuration, launcher, and audit are privately preserved. Archive SHA-256: `61671f943850c0601a9febb3058bf3e1e2df3689b7ef06594280aa89ce087c9f`. No Daytona sandboxes remain.

The teacher uses native Pi 0.87.0, matching the runtime pin in [evaluation policy #9409](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9409), with the [Skill2Env paper, section 3.4](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env/blob/main/paper/Skill2Env_arXiv.pdf) teacher budget: 131,072 total context tokens, a 32,768-token solver output cap, high thinking, and native compaction. Pi's high setting maps to GLM chat-template thinking enabled; no provider `reasoning_effort` tier is sent. BixBench policy instead uses 32,768 total context and 8,192 output tokens; collection and evaluation budgets remain separate. Live requests obeyed the configured cap, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and repetition seeds 0–4. The largest observed prompt was 98,346 tokens; compaction used a 16,384-token output cap. This is not a full context-boundary stress test.

Execution uses upstream Harbor `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3` with a configuration-only adapter around Pi. Native tools, prompt, loop, task resources, and component grades are retained. Setup allows the recorded package mirrors; agent execution allows the scoped model endpoint, and verification retains the task's no-network policy. The initial six-task collection used at most three concurrent trials, native 30-minute agent timeouts, a six-hour batch limit, and no whole-trial retries. The expanded batch retains native timeouts and task resources, with the concurrency and batch limit recorded above. Frozen protocol SHA-256: `33a9e03a0a426b9d1ed8c328f2743ec4efa9b0fdf4425907d4f93dce156aa338`. BixBench-overlap checking is not a prerequisite.

Before SFT, recover available recorded content, validate native-format conversion and loss masks, and count supervised tokens. Keep output limits, repeated tool loops, missing exports, and grader diagnostics as annotations. Pin the selected parent weights and tokenizer, validate the chosen training recipe and long-conversation handling, and freeze the BixBench evaluation protocol. No training or BixBench comparison has run.

## Links

- [Completed Pi collection and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6006473943).
- Logbook: dated updates in this issue; keep this body current as decisions change.
- W&B report: pending the first training run.
- Dataset assessment and known grader issue: [#9630](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9630).
- Biology evaluation protocols and baselines: [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258).
- Source project: [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env).

## Decision Log

- 2026-10-05: Start with released Skill2Env biology tasks and complete GLM-only demonstrations. Use native component rewards to select traces and assistant-only SFT. Defer relay methods.
- 2026-10-05: Treat general scientific data analysis as a possible expansion if the validated biology pool is insufficient.
- 2026-10-05: Track this experiment here and link its evaluation results from #9258. Preserve Atlas intake under #9630.
- 2026-10-05: Completed reference/no-op controls on six pinned tasks. Collection: five attempts per task, 30 total. Treat rewards as graded vectors and choose the SFT selection policy after inspecting pilot distributions; this supersedes earlier binary verified-success wording.

- 2026-10-05: Authorized the 30-rollout collection and removed BixBench-overlap checking as a prerequisite. Preserve source provenance and full component rewards.
- 2026-10-05: Superseded Terminus-2 with Pi to match the intended Snowball harness. Selected the paper's 128k context / 32k output teacher budget if supported. Retain the seven prior attempts separately; do not resume their queue.

- 2026-10-06: Completed the 30-attempt Pi batch with 29 native reward vectors and 17 normal trace candidates. Preserve all native scores and raw captures; keep output-limit endings, timeouts, and the ungraded infrastructure failure separate. SFT selection and training remain pending.

- 2026-10-06: Authorized five attempts for every remaining shortlisted biology task (262 tasks; 1,310 new attempts) while unattended. Selected 64 concurrent rollouts after checking bulk inference guidance and sandbox quota. Preserve every native reward vector and verified private artifacts; defer SFT selection and training.

- 2026-10-06: Recovered the first expanded job's 46 fallback attempts without changing native grades. Continue only the 435 unattempted slots; replace the short capture-close window with a bounded 35-minute wait outside the upload lock. Preserve all prior attempts, including incomplete and ungraded outcomes.

- 2026-10-06: Completed all 1,310 expanded slots without duplicates; all evidence is retained and continuation sandbox cleanup is complete. Keep the issue open for the planned SFT and evaluation stages.

- 2026-10-06: Selected an unfiltered first SFT baseline using all available GLM/Pi solver traces, including truncated and interrupted prefixes; supersedes earlier reward and completeness selection proposals. Preserve scores as annotations and avoid artificial termination targets. GitHub and Discord precedents support a bounded continuation but leave parent, mixture, and hyperparameters open.

- 2026-10-06: Selected September 21 Datakit SFT, biology traces only with no replay, one run at peak LR 1e-4, three epochs, 131,072-token training sequences, and effective global batch 16. Save/export and evaluate the final model only; per-epoch checkpointing was dropped because of model-size overhead.

- 2026-10-06: Confirmed full-parameter SFT with fresh AdamH (betas 0.9/0.95, epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0, clip 1.0), 3% warmup, cosine decay from 1e-4 to 1e-5, and frozen imported router biases. Start evaluation with BixBench alone; decide on other evaluations after its result.

- 2026-10-06: Selected reconstructed conversations and CoreWeave H100 compute (32 GPUs). Finalized 5,120 windows with 73,894,261 supervised tokens per epoch; batch 16 and three epochs give 960 steps. All 58 preparation artifacts passed full SHA-256 readback. Preserve every available solver output, crop only masked context where necessary, and finish trainer validation before launch.

## Conclusion

Collection and the agreed three-epoch, biology-only SFT run are complete. Pi is the primary evaluation harness because it matches teacher collection and intended deployment. The current Pi/BixBench diagnostic does not establish an SFT improvement: thinking-enabled accuracy was parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5, and thinking-disabled SFT has only two graded attempts out of five. An unexecuted tool call in the final parsed reasoning field was observed in one of five thinking-enabled parent traces and all five SFT traces. It is a pre-existing failure pattern that appeared more frequently after SFT in this sample; it is not unique to the SFT checkpoint. The small sample and incomplete grading limit any broader accuracy claim.

This experiment is finished at the owner's request. The unresolved cause of the Pi formatting behavior and the three missing thinking-disabled SFT grades are accepted limitations of the final result, not outstanding work under this issue. No further runs or debugging are planned here. Any future experiment would have a separate scope and should use Pi as its primary evaluation harness.

Terminus-2 and synthetic tasks remain secondary diagnostics. The [completed prompt ablation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083809697) accepted 36/36 parent versus 0/36 SFT first responses under the Terminus schema. These findings do not establish a remedy for the primary Pi failures. Results and analysis are preserved, and the final diagnostic inference servers have stopped.

comments.body:
🤖 Prepared the first biology validation batch: DepMap, pysam, CELLxGENE, scikit-bio, PyDESeq2, and Scanpy. All 105 downloaded files match the Harbor release metadata hashes. This is static inspection and launch preparation; no validation trials, GLM calls, or training jobs have run.

The batch has 12 sequential trials: one native no-op control and one supplied reference solution per task. It uses [Harbor `bf991e4`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3), preserving each task's 2 CPUs, 4 GiB RAM, 4 GiB storage, offline runtime policy, and native time limits. The batch has a three-hour wall-time limit, no experiment retries, and sandbox deletion after each trial. Incomplete trials remain separate from task failures.

A reference must pass every native reward component; the no-op must not fully pass. Some test wrappers emit zero rewards after grader errors, so component scores alone cannot establish a valid negative control. Preserve and inspect verifier logs. Static inspection also found potential timing pressure in the Scanpy and PyDESeq2 graders; execution will determine whether their native 600-second verifier limit is sufficient.

The local bundle passes syntax, file-set, hash, and task-configuration checks. Sandbox execution has not started; account billing coverage is being checked. Public list prices do not establish an additional cash cost for this account. BixBench overlap checks and training-data licensing review remain before collecting the SFT dataset.

# Research

The 268 biology candidates are a metadata shortlist, and the prepared six-task batch has passed file and hash checks but no reference or no-op trial has run. Task validity, training/evaluation overlap, licenses, and the Snowball before/after baseline remain open. [PR #9632](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9632) covers Atlas intake only; the regressions in [#9719](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9719) and evaluation variability in [#9558](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9558) make a bounded, paired SFT test important.

Data quality, formatting, dose, and parent choice need measurement.

Proposed recipe, pending parent selection and token accounting:

- Parent: recommend the shared September 21 Datakit SFT checkpoint; pin weights, tokenizer, and its own thinking/tool chat template together. The parent is not yet fixed.
- Data: review high-scoring complete traces first; allow partial credit through an explicit component-based policy. Exclude malformed, looping, interrupted, or grader-invalid candidates from the initial training pool. Balance task families and deduplicate near-identical solutions. Hold out 10–15% of task families before sequence construction; all repetitions and segments of a task stay in one split.
- Targets: preserve main-agent reasoning, tool calls, final answers, and end-of-turn tokens; mask system/user/tool observations. Render GLM/Pi messages in Snowball's native format. Count each assistant target once. Keep auxiliary compaction generation outside the initial target set and preserve its resulting summary when it is part of the actual solver context.
- Training: full-parameter fine-tuning with fresh Adam state; betas 0.9/0.95, epsilon 1e-8, clip 1, weight decay 0, BF16 compute, frozen router bias. Start at LR 1e-5 with 5% warmup and cosine decay to 1e-6. These LR and warmup choices are conservative proposals, not a previously successful biology setting. A later 3e-5 arm can test sensitivity.
- Budget: one pass initially, save at approximately quarter/half/full exposure; extend to two passes only if held-out behavior improves. Target 65,536-token examples and effective batch 16, subject to memory validation. Inspect target coverage before finalizing length. Long traces require context-preserving examples at valid turn or compaction boundaries; do not silently truncate them. Use separate examples until the selected implementation proves packed-document isolation. Derive steps from the actual sequence cache, not provider usage totals.

Replay is an ablation. The [September 21 parent card](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21) records 20% long-context pretraining replay, but that does not establish the required fraction for this short continuation. Compare biology-only with 80% biology / 20% audited general SFT replay, at equal biology-token exposure and the same optimizer/schedule. Use token-based allocation and log both processed and loss-bearing tokens. General replay should cover reasoning, instruction following, and compatible tool use. Raw pretraining replay would be a separate arm with full next-token loss; it is most useful to test if broad or long-context retention regresses.

Before training: freeze the parent, audit graders and target formatting, compute unique target and context-token counts with Snowball's tokenizer, then validate one update, checkpoint export, and Pi tool-call parsing. Evaluate parent and selected intermediate checkpoints with identical Pi budgets on biology development tasks and BixBench, plus instruction-following, code/math, and long-context retention checks. Use development results for tuning and reserve the final benchmark comparison. GPU allocation and spend remain to be specified after sequence accounting.

🤖 Heads-up from marin#9920: the HF export in this recipe will fail at the final step unless patched.

`train.py` sets `model_ref` to the regional S3 copy of the parent (`ctx.artifact_path(parent)`), and `train_lm` passes that through as the converter's `reference_checkpoint`. The HF export hook calls `save_pretrained` without `save_reference_code`, which resolves to True for Snowball because `GrugMoeHfConfig` is not a `transformers` class. `_save_code_local` then calls raw `hf_hub_download(repo_id="s3://...")` and raises `HFValidationError` before the config, tokenizer and shard index are written. We hit exactly this on 2026-10-07 at 23:57 UTC in a CruxEval SFT run with the same recipe (marin#9920).

Since this run exports only once (`hf_save_steps=steps + 1`) with native checkpoints disabled (`save_interval=None`, `save_final_checkpoint=False`), a 960-step run would end with nothing saved. Fixes under discussion in #9920: plumb `save_reference_code=False` through `AdaptorExportConfig` → `save_hf_checkpoint_callback` → `save_pretrained` (the parent repo has no code files, so nothing is lost), or make `_save_code_local` URL-aware like the load paths.

🤖 Reproduced two Grug streaming-parser defects against the pinned vLLM source and submitted matched two-question checks with a tested fix.

1. The parser can interpret an earlier assistant turn's end-think marker as closing the new turn's reasoning. This exposes new reasoning as ordinary text.

This establishes that both checkpoints can solve this real task under mini-swe-agent, and SFT can solve it under Pi with thinking off. One question and one attempt per condition do not establish general benchmark performance.

### Controlled short-prompt check

Each checkpoint received the same brief prompt asking it to start by calling bash to read a CSV, ten times per thinking setting (temperature 0.7, seeds 0–9). No tool was executed in this check. A valid response means a parsed bash tool call with JSON arguments containing a string command.

| Setting | Parent valid tool calls | Biology SFT valid tool calls |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Thinking on | 10/10 | 3/10 |
| Thinking off | 10/10 | 10/10 |

Raw decoded streaming output was matched to all forty response IDs. All seven SFT thinking-on failures placed tool blocks inside unclosed reasoning. Each had only 195 prompt tokens and generated 25–66 tokens, with finish reason `stop`, not `length`. These failures therefore do not require long context or exhausting a token limit. The SFT Pi thinking-on BixBench attempt showed the same pattern at 1,651 input / 27 output tokens.

Four SFT thinking-off outputs also contained unclosed reasoning markers with tool blocks, although the API returned valid tools. Disabling thinking changes how these outputs are handled; it does not demonstrate that generation itself is repaired. The exact training or serialization cause remains unproven.

### Protocol and evidence

Both models used 32,768 context / 8,192 output, the same Grug reasoning and Hermes tool parsers, Pi 1.1.0 or mini-swe-agent 2.1.0, and Harbor `0985d012bcf4cc9d1acb1a831a86350cd31ac72a`. The task came from `bixbench-cli-marin-corrections@3`, with 300-second agent and verifier limits. It was selected using a prior correct GLM-5.3 / Terminus-2 attempt taking 18.68 agent seconds; that historical timing is only a selection heuristic.

Source/config archive:
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/teacher-traces/skill2env-bio-sft-20261006/short-bixbench-source-20261008.tar.gz`

`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/teacher-traces/skill2env-bio-sft-20261006/short-bixbench-results-20261008.tar.gz`

Native traces and verifier artifacts remain under the individual run IDs at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/`. Raw decoded text is available; token-ID arrays were not captured. No further runs launched.

🤖 Launching the authorized extension: five additional historically short BixBench questions, matched across parent and biology SFT under Pi thinking-on, Pi thinking-off, and mini-swe-agent thinking-on. Thirty attempts total, one per task/model/setting, no retries.

No correctness filter; all five selected attempts happened to grade correct. Historical runtimes exclude setup and grading and are selection evidence, not predictions for these checkpoints. [Historical run](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5765246487).

Same protocol as the preceding one-question comparison: pinned CLI-corrections v3 tasks, Harbor 0985d012bcf4cc9d1acb1a831a86350cd31ac72a, Pi 1.1.0 / mini-swe-agent 2.1.0, 32,768 context / 8,192 output, 300-second agent and verifier limits, and concurrency one per model. One eight-H100 server per checkpoint with normal batch teardown. The fixed short-prompt diagnostic is not repeated. | mini-swe-agent, thinking on | 2 correct / 5 graded | 1 correct / 5 graded |

These are five historically short questions with one attempt per setting, not a representative benchmark score. [Selection and fixed protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6068487263).

| Question | Parent Pi on | Parent Pi off | Parent MSA | SFT Pi on | SFT Pi off | SFT MSA |

The parent executed tools in all ten Pi attempts and answered proteomics correctly in both settings. This is direct evidence that the parent can use Pi, although it performs poorly on this small subset.

All five SFT Pi-thinking-on traces ended with tool-call markup returned in the API's reasoning content rather than an executable tool call. Two executed no tools; the other three executed 9, 2 and 23 tool results before stopping. Final requests had 1,643–14,421 input tokens and 64–308 output tokens, with stop reason `stop`. This repeats the earlier formatting symptom without exhausting either configured token limit. This observation is from saved Pi/API traces; raw decoded output was not re-audited for this batch.

Timeouts and limits matter:

- Three SFT Pi-off attempts have `VerifierTimeoutError` and no grade. That block has only 40% grading coverage and its evaluation record is `infra_failed`; no accuracy metric was published for it. The SFT root exited with `1 of 3 evals failed: bix-pi-nothink (infra_failed)` after completing the other blocks and teardown.
- Parent Pi-on logistic regression, parent Pi-off methylation, and SFT MSA CRISPR carry primary `AgentTimeoutError`; each nevertheless has a saved zero grade.
- The reused MSA configuration has a 30-step cap as well as the 300-second agent limit. Native `LimitsExceeded` endings occurred on parent phylogenetics/CRISPR and SFT phylogenetics/logistic regression/methylation. These are not all tool-format failures.

The completed comparisons do not show a broad SFT improvement. Changing the harness helps some tasks, but does not resolve the whole problem. The most specific reproducible lead remains SFT's thinking-on output formatting. Inspecting the training serialization and matched traces is more informative next than launching another larger benchmark. Verifier timeouts need separate investigation before interpreting the Pi-off comparison.

🤖 Saved-data audit found no missing-reasoning-boundary conversion bug. No model calls, GPU work, training changes, or new evaluations were made.

I streamed all 5,120 published training rows, inspected every supervised target after accounting for next-token loss alignment, and verified the input file SHA256 against the published-source manifest (`9fcb0157bab9a5cfcadd13effac30b9bc675a5958fce82fc5aa7d71162934976`).

| Check | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Supervised outputs | 66,741 |
| Supervised tokens | 73,894,261 |
| Tool-call opening tags in targets | 75,153 |
| Tool-call tags inside an unclosed reasoning block | 0 |
| Supervised reasoning-closing tokens | 14,012 |
| End-of-turn tokens inside unfinished reasoning | 0 |

There are 295 targets ending in unfinished reasoning (0.44%), consistent with retaining truncated prefixes without inventing an end-of-turn token. These targets contain no tool calls inside that reasoning. This audit does not demonstrate that truncated examples are harmless, but they do not directly teach the observed tool-call-inside-reasoning ending.

52,434 targets (78.56%) contain no reasoning block. Replaying 1,111 original captured solver outputs from the first ten lexically ordered initial archives confirmed that absent reasoning was already absent in the teacher response: 992 tool-call outputs had no teacher reasoning. All 110 sampled outputs containing both reasoning and tool calls rendered a reasoning-closing marker before their tool calls. Twenty saved finalized rows matched reconstructed token arrays and shifted loss masks exactly.

The preparation/finalization source hashes match the original published code. Parent and exported SFT serving templates are byte-identical. The training template's only difference from serving is the default reasoning-mode header when no explicit mode is supplied; prompt rendering explicitly enables thinking, and isolated target rendering omits that extra system header. The suspected `edit` schema also matches: collection and Pi 1.1.0 use `path` and `edits[]`.

Interpretation: the simplest serialization hypothesis is not supported. This is not a full end-to-end training correctness proof: I did not read back the remote token cache or run a GPU forward pass. A possible learning issue is the mixture of many direct-tool targets and fewer reasoning-plus-tool targets under thinking-enabled prompts, but that is a hypothesis, not an established cause or reason to filter the dataset yet.

Terminus-2 remains a useful independent harness control. The [pinned implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/0985d012bcf4cc9d1acb1a831a86350cd31ac72a/src/harbor/agents/terminus_2/terminus_2.py#L2348) parses commands from text rather than using native API tool calling. Existing saved synthetic results confirm 8/10 parent and 7/10 SFT with thinking off. It has not yet been run on the five runtime-selected BixBench questions. A matched ten-attempt comparison would distinguish some harness sensitivity from broader task-performance problems; it would not establish the cause of the learned delimiter regression.

Audit code, counts, sampled replay evidence, source pins and limitations:
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/teacher-traces/skill2env-bio-sft-20261006/serialization-audit-20261008.tar.gz`

🤖 Submitted the Terminus-2 comparison: the same five historically short BixBench questions, one attempt each for the parent and bio-SFT checkpoints (10 attempts total).

- Tasks: `bix-37-q4`, `bix-52-q7`, `bix-6-q4`, `bix-51-q2`, `bix-34-q2`. Selection and historical runtimes are unchanged from the previous comparison; no correctness filtering.
- Terminus-2, thinking disabled, 32,768-token context, 8,192-token output, 300-second agent and verifier limits, no retries, one concurrent trial per model.
- Same pinned Harbor revision, task snapshot and Together judge as the preceding Pi/MSA comparison. Each model uses an eight-H100 inference server with automatic teardown after its batch.
- Both root jobs and their inference children were running at 21:55 UTC on October 8. This is startup confirmation, not a completed evaluation result.

Parent job: `/exedev/eval-20261008-215115-skill2env-bio-9775-parent-terminus-bixbench-0a6f`

SFT job: `/exedev/eval-20261008-215128-skill2env-bio-9775-final-terminus-bixbench-09e8`

Run IDs:
- `20261008-215115-skill2env-bio-9775-parent-terminus-bixbench-bix-terminus-nothink-ab11`
- `20261008-215128-skill2env-bio-9775-final-terminus-bixbench-bix-terminus-nothink-9774`

Configurations, task-selection provenance and submission receipts: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/teacher-traces/skill2env-bio-sft-20261006/terminus-bixbench-source-20261008.tar.gz`.

This tests whether Terminus-2's text-based command protocol works better than native tool calls on these real questions. Correctness and infrastructure failures will be reported separately.

🤖 Terminus-2 completed all ten BixBench attempts: parent 1/5 correct, bio-SFT 0/5. All attempts were graded; the parent had one agent timeout and SFT had five. Both batch roots succeeded and both inference children have stopped. The trace analysis identifies a response-schema regression on these prompts, with reasoning-channel problems affecting a smaller subset.

| Question | Parent correct | SFT correct | SFT parser-error turns / agent turns | First SFT turn with commands |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `bix-34-q2` | 0 | 0 | 188/188 | Never |
| `bix-37-q4` | 1 | 0 | 174/174 | Never |
| `bix-51-q2` | 0 | 0 | 183/183 | Never |
| `bix-52-q7` | 0 | 0 | 13/39 | 3 |
| `bix-6-q4` | 0 | 0 | 5/17 | 2 |

Terminus asks for JSON with `analysis`, `plan`, and `commands`. On the proteomics task, the SFT model instead returned this exact string on 173 of 174 turns:

```text
<tool_call>
{"name": "bash", "arguments": {"command": "ls -la /workspace/"}}
</tool_call>
```

Every turn received feedback identifying the missing fields. The other two zero-command runs mostly emitted `keystrokes`/`duration` objects inside `<tool_call>` tags, still missing the required outer structure. Across these three runs, 541 of 545 turns failed with missing fields; four had empty visible content and tool markup in reasoning. Simply exposing reasoning as content would leave the dominant schema failure unresolved. Removing the tags alone would also leave the missing fields.

The failure starts at 918–961 input tokens and 74–95 generated tokens on the first call, before any dataset is read. Long context is not needed to trigger it. The recorded initial prompts for these three tasks are identical between parent and SFT after replacing sandbox UUIDs. The parent executes commands on its first turn on all five tasks. The only initial-prompt difference beyond UUIDs across the five pairs is the terminal shell-prompt line on CRISPR.

There is evidence against complete loss of Terminus capability: the earlier synthetic comparison scored parent 8/10 and SFT 7/10, and two current SFT tasks recovered enough to execute commands. These observations support prompt-sensitive format adherence. They do not establish which prompt component triggers the failure, nor a general biological reasoning regression.

Training evidence provides a candidate explanation. The [published-input audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069710545) counted tool-call markup in 65,481/66,741 supervised spans (98.1%). This is a span fraction, not a token fraction or count of independent examples. The targets teach Pi-style native tool calls, not Terminus command JSON. The raw-source replay contains the same `name: bash` / `arguments: command` format seen above. Concentration on this format could reduce adherence to another protocol, but this is not a causal finding. The prior audit found zero supervised tool tags inside open reasoning and no forced end-of-turn inside open reasoning; it does not support a simple missing-delimiter conversion bug. It also did not verify the remote training cache or GPU forward pass.

Next, prioritize a small first-response prompt ablation before more full BixBench rollouts: use the saved initial prompts for the three zero-command cases, both checkpoints, fixed decoding, and change one component at a time (remove notebook/answer-file boilerplate; replace the biological question with a neutral directory-listing request; add one valid Terminus JSON example). Score required-schema compliance and reasoning/content placement separately. Keep these as diagnostics, not tuned benchmark scores. Pi remains the intended deployment harness; a Terminus workaround alone would not resolve the prior Pi failures. If a training follow-up is needed, change one factor first (training exposure or a format-preservation mixture), rather than changing learning rate, duration, and data simultaneously.

No new model calls, GPU jobs, or training were launched for this analysis. Successful trajectory steps contain Harbor-normalized analysis/plan text; parser-error steps preserve API content and reasoning fields. These are not raw token IDs. The five-task sample and single attempt per checkpoint do not support a general benchmark conclusion.

[Launch/configuration record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069794183). Same pinned Harbor/task versions, 32k context/8k output, thinking disabled, 300-second agent/verifier limits, no retries.

The analysis and reproduction script have been archived with the experiment artifacts.

🤖 The controlled first-response ablation is running. The bio-SFT half has completed: the exact pinned Terminus parser accepts 0/36 responses. The parent control is still copying its checkpoint after a cache miss; no parent result is available yet.

The matrix uses the three previously selected zero-command prompts and four variants: original, removal of notebook/answer-file instructions, replacement of the biological question with a neutral directory-listing request, and addition of a valid Terminus JSON example. Each variant has one greedy response and two sampled responses (temperature 0.7, seeds 0 and 1). All calls disable thinking and cap output at 1,024 tokens. These are direct first-response API diagnostics, not exact replays of the original decoding settings and not benchmark scores. No commands are executed.

All four SFT variants have 0/9 accepted responses. Six of the 36 hit the output limit; the remaining 30 stopped normally and still failed. All responses have nonempty content; none has a separate reasoning field. The pinned parser reports 26 missing-field errors and ten responses without valid JSON. In 24 responses, individual command objects can be decoded and their keystrokes end with the required newline, but the required outer schema is absent.

These specific prompt edits have not fixed SFT format adherence. The neutral-task failures also mean biological subject matter is not necessary for the observed failure. Full comparison and conclusions will follow after the parent control completes. Exact requests, streamed responses, diagnostic code, and parser replay are preserved with the experiment artifacts.

🤖 Clarification to the Pi interpretation: the tool-call-in-reasoning ending also occurs in the parent. In the matched five-question thinking-enabled batch, the final saved response contains an unexecuted tool call in the reasoning field in **1/5 parent attempts versus 5/5 SFT attempts**. These counts describe final responses, not a count of every formatting anomaly throughout each trajectory.

The affected parent attempt is `bix-37-q4`: it had already written the correct answer, then emitted a `read` call for the answer file inside reasoning and stopped. It therefore still scored 1. All five SFT attempts scored 0; two executed no tools, while three executed tools before the problematic ending.

The issue summary and conclusion now state that this is a pre-existing failure pattern observed more frequently after SFT in this small sample. The teacher collection used thinking enabled throughout: Pi's high setting mapped to `enable_thinking=true`, and the collection proxy rejected requests without it. Thinking-disabled student evaluation is a diagnostic, not a second teacher-data condition.

🤖 The secondary Terminus prompt ablation is complete: the pinned Terminus parser accepts **36/36 parent responses and 0/36 SFT responses**. Both jobs succeeded and both inference servers have stopped. Pi remains the primary evaluation; this measures transfer to Terminus's response schema, not BixBench answer accuracy.

| Prompt variant | Parent accepted | SFT accepted | SFT output-limit stops |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Original saved prompt | 9/9 | 0/9 | 2/9 |
| Remove notebook/answer-file instructions | 9/9 | 0/9 | 0/9 |
| Replace biological question with directory listing | 9/9 | 0/9 | 4/9 |
| Add a valid Terminus JSON example | 9/9 | 0/9 | 0/9 |

Each row covers three selected prompts (`bix-34-q2`, `bix-37-q4`, `bix-51-q2`), with one greedy response and two sampled responses per prompt. The sampled settings are temperature 0.7, seeds 0 and 1. Both checkpoints received identical prompts with thinking disabled, a 32k serving context, and a 1,024-token output cap. These are 72 first-response calls, not 72 independent tasks; no commands were executed. The questions were chosen because their original SFT attempts executed no commands.

The exact parser from pinned Harbor revision `0985d012bcf4cc9d1acb1a831a86350cd31ac72a` confirms the initial structural checker: parent 36 accepted responses with commands, SFT zero. SFT has 26 missing-field errors and ten responses with no valid JSON. Six hit the output cap; all 30 normally stopped responses still fail. All SFT responses contain visible content; none uses a separate reasoning field in this direct API diagnostic. In 24 responses, individual `keystrokes` objects can be decoded with correct trailing newlines, but the required outer `analysis`/`plan`/`commands` structure is absent. Thus these failures cannot be fixed simply by exposing reasoning as content or removing tool-call tags.

The tested prompt edits do not restore Terminus format adherence. Biological subject matter is not necessary: the neutral-question variant also fails for SFT. This supports reduced adherence to an alternative command protocol after this SFT run. It does not establish the cause of the Pi failures, general loss of tool capability, or a biological reasoning regression. Earlier SFT success on 7/10 synthetic Terminus tasks remains relevant counterevidence to a blanket capability-loss claim.

The primary Pi interpretation is unchanged by this secondary test: [the final unexecuted-tool-call-in-reasoning pattern occurs in both checkpoints](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083719436), in 1/5 parent versus 5/5 SFT thinking-enabled attempts. The teacher was collected with thinking enabled throughout; disabling student thinking is a diagnostic. Further mitigation should be judged on Pi first. These Terminus results do not justify treating a Terminus prompt workaround as the primary objective.

Exact prompts, streamed API responses, decoding settings, per-response classifications, the pinned parser and replay script, hashes, and completion state are archived with the experiment artifacts. The direct API settings differ from the original full agent run (explicit decoding and shorter output cap), so this is a controlled diagnostic rather than an exact replay. No new training was launched. The parent cache miss delayed startup; future diagnostics can reuse the previously verified regional parent copy.

🤖 Closing this experiment as completed at the owner's request, with a negative primary result: the tested biology-only SFT recipe did not demonstrate improved Pi/BixBench performance.

With thinking enabled, the matched five-question comparison scored parent 1/5 and SFT 0/5. The problematic final tool-call-in-reasoning pattern occurred in both checkpoints (parent 1/5, SFT 5/5). The small sample, unresolved cause, and three missing grades in the thinking-disabled SFT comparison remain limitations; they are not prerequisites to closing this experiment. Terminus results are secondary diagnostics.

The issue body records the final conclusion, configurations, results, and analysis links. No further training, evaluation, or debugging is planned under this issue. No follow-up issue is being opened as part of this closure.

topics.title: [grug] Keep AdamH updates finite on zero-norm matrices
topics.body:
scale_by_adamh projects onto the parameter's Frobenius sphere by dividing by
the updated matrix norm. A zero matrix stays zero through a zero learning-rate
or zero-gradient step, so the division is 0/0 and the update is NaN. Floor
that norm at 1e-10, the same floor the direction step already uses.

Fixes #9054

topics.title: [grafana] Prepare GPU history by requested priority
topics.body:
Prepare seven-day H100 and Blackwell (GB200) allocation-history panels grouped by each child job's requested priority. An Interactive request dispatched as Batch stays in the Interactive group. There is no applied-priority lookup or toggle. Iris and Finelog server code, persisted schemas, retention and writes are unchanged.

The projection sums requested GPU sizes over recorded attempt execution intervals at common sampling instants, with cadence chosen from the selected range: one minute through six hours, five minutes through two days, and fifteen minutes through seven days. Exact historical pod binding/cleanup intervals and allocatable capacity remain unavailable. The requested-GPU series therefore recovers only part of allocation; every point is marked incomplete and idle stays blank. Missing regional inputs leave blank spans. Coverage compares Finelog per-root Running task counts with retained attempt intervals, including CPU tasks; differences flag incomplete or inconsistent task history. It also reports setup tasks and unresolved GPU models. Without assignment creation times, the reader cannot establish when setup began, so setup GPU quantities stay blank.

The production metadata reader remains to be implemented and wired; without one the bridge returns HTTP 503. An approved temporary pilot used Grafana's actual CW service identity plus five-minute Iris dashboard-role cookies over the public Kubernetes controller proxy in all three regions. Existing job/resource/full-retry reads succeeded, GetCurrentUser reported dashboard, and SELECT1 was denied by Iris with HTTP 403. All temporary Role/RoleBinding objects were deleted and absence verified; Grafana's original proxy403 returned afterward. No production grants, credentials or deployment remain from the pilot. The minimal tested transport scope is services/proxy on iris/iris-controller-svc:10000; this reader's POST RPCs need the Kubernetes create verb, plus separate read-only Iris authentication.

A straightforward job/task-API reader would require at least 44,398 inventory calls over the captured sampled cohort, before additional pages and full-retry calls. This is a request-count estimate, not measured production latency. Existing controller backups offer a possible bulk alternative without controller changes: recent backups exist in all three regions. One GB200 backup was 25.4 MB compressed and 421.6 MB decompressed; it downloaded in 1.17s, decompressed in 0.22s, and returned 5,712 retained attempts in a 0.032s immutable local SQL query on devbox. Regional coverage, Cloud Run memory/refresh cost, and scoped object-read credentials still need validation before choosing and wiring that reader. Existing backups already contain requested band and current task band; older attempts do not have their own applied-band field.

All 421 Grafana tests and pre-commit checks passed. The requested-only preview uses captured task-state and regional metadata, with 672 common fifteen-minute instants per model. Every point is incomplete; 226 instants show a difference between per-root Running counts and retained intervals. Earlier applied-view replay timings are retained as prior measurements; production requested-reader loading and refresh costs remain unmeasured.

topics.title: [grug] Raise Snowball MFU on AMD Instinct GPUs
topics.body:
## TL;DR

MI350X best: 14.31% MFU (`ring_dedup` + gather combine + ROCm top-k + flash attention + new `ragged_dot`, bf16, batch 64, `save_moe` remat, 1.580 s per step). Before the MoE changes: 12.70% (batch 96, `save_moe`, 2.670 s). All from clean compiles.
MI300X best: 10.3% MFU at batch 32 (unconfirmed: hung at step 10); confirmed 8.66% at batch 16.

## Description

#9462 got the full 67B-A2B Snowball (June) model training on one 8-GPU AMD node. This issue tracks raising its MFU, mainly on MI350X, with MI300X as the reference. Each experiment gets one comment with the commit, the exact command and the result; the tables below index those comments and are edited as results land.

Shared setup, unless a row says otherwise: full June model, one 8-GPU node, EP8 (`--expert-axis 8`), reference attention, `ring` MoE backend, 4096 context, synthetic tokens, XLA command buffers off. Benchmark script: `experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py` (#9693, not yet merged). Slurm wrapper: [`run_gpu.sh`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6018393879) (to be committed).

MFU is against AMD's dense bf16 peak (MI300X 1,307 TFLOP/s, MI350X 2,307 TFLOP/s).

## MI350X

Baseline: bf16, Triton `ragged_dot` (`RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton`), batch 8, default memory fraction.

| GPU | Change from baseline | Batch | Step | Tokens/s | MFU | Peak mem | Commit | Details |

| MI350X | baseline | 8 | 0.73 s | 45,000 | 3.88% | 164.3 GiB | 9c0d02a | [link](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6018574870) |
| MI350X | fp16, XLA `ragged_dot` | 8 | 1.08 s | 30,400 | 2.62% | 149.9 GiB | 9c0d02a | [link](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6018574870) |
| MI350X | fp16, XLA `ragged_dot` | 16 | 2.00 s | 32,800 | 2.82% | 153.8 GiB | 9c0d02a | [link](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6018574870) |

# Research

MI350X reaches 3.86% MFU with bf16 Triton `ragged_dot`; its fp16 XLA runs reach 2.59–2.83%. The reported ~10 ms Triton expert matmul is a bottleneck hypothesis; the current MI350X results do not include a pinned-revision profile that attributes the full step. MI300X batch 32 reached 10.3% MFU over steps 2–9 but hung at step 10, which coincides with the trainer's watch interval; the cause and sustained throughput remain unconfirmed.

**Relevant code**
- [`synthetic_benchmark.py#L92-L108`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f8627e501110959b00c92ce30452bfaf780c95d9/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py#L92-L108) — benchmark flags; no watch control
- [`synthetic_benchmark.py#L145-L166`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f8627e501110959b00c92ce30452bfaf780c95d9/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py#L145-L166) — trainer uses default watch configuration
- [`train.py#L641-L649`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/train.py#L641-L649) — interval selects watch computation
- [`ragged_dot.py#L341-L367`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py#L341-L367) — XLA/Triton selection

# Proposed Fix

1. Extend the existing benchmark PR #9693 with a benchmark-only watch interval flag (0 disables watch) and the Slurm wrapper used in the issue. Pin one post-rebase benchmark commit and the ROCm/JAX versions for every comparison. Keep the production watch default unchanged.
2. On 8× MI300X, rerun the full EP8 batch-32 configuration for 20 steps with watch intervals 10 and 0, `RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=xla`, memory fraction 0.90, no profiler, and command buffers off. Record the step-10 outcome, median time over non-watch steps 2–9 and 11–19, tokens/s, MFU, and peak memory. Treat 10.3% as preliminary until a 20-step run completes; if both variants hang, capture the failing step's trace before changing the model.
3. At the same pinned commit, rerun MI350X bf16/Triton batch 8 and fp16/XLA batches 8, 16, and 32 with the same 20-step setup. Profile a separate run of the fastest completed configuration and report time in expert GEMMs, collectives, other kernels, and host gaps. Compare against the MI300X reference only after these reruns.
4. Use that profile to choose one next change: test `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all` if communication dominates, or tune the Triton expert GEMM if it dominates. Test command-buffer types separately on a smaller shape with finite-loss checks before a full-model run; the [current ROCm setup](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/559) has produced non-finite gradients and crashes with command buffers enabled. Post each run's commit, exact command, job ID, step time, MFU, peak memory, and negative results here.

Completion criterion: a full 20-step MI350X run with finite loss and a measured improvement over the rerun bf16/Triton batch-8 baseline (previously 3.86%). #9777 already covers ROCm architecture parsing; RCCL ragged all-to-all remains unsupported in its reported test, so it is not a parallel implementation target for this issue.

🤖 ### MI350X bf16 matmul ceiling: 1,229 TFLOP/s in JAX by kernel time (53% of datasheet peak, 97% of PyTorch's sustained 1,261)

Commits: 265ea0f (MAMF jobs 453328, 453329), d733a95 (453334), 52cf1ee (JAX 453412), 08516a7 (JAX 453420, 453421), 6b47d18 (JAX 454529), 370d41d (JAX 454561), 704ceff (JAX 454577-454580) · GPU: one MI350X or MI300X, whole node reserved · Scripts: [`experiments/amd/matmul_ceiling`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/63b08883fd1c77de655310ef7c050950533b69a9/experiments/amd/matmul_ceiling) (PR #9840)

This measures how fast one GPU runs a plain dense matmul, to give the MFU numbers above a measured ceiling. Two tools ran on the same node for each GPU type: k007-002 for MI350X, k002-003 for MI300X. Both venvs install AMD's `rocm-sdk-libraries==10.0.0` wheel, which provides hipBLASLt and rocBLAS; the nodes' system ROCm (`/opt/rocm-7.2.0`) is not used for compute.

- Stas Bekman's [MAMF-finder](https://github.com/stas00/ml-engineering/blob/0359db89793c313e90e4f8a8bc8a2b1514ba00ae/compute/accelerator/benchmarks/mamf-finder.py) (PyTorch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=1`, which benchmarks every rocBLAS and hipBLASLt solution per shape and keeps the fastest) searches about 2,100 shapes. It reports MAMF (maximum achievable matmul FLOPS): the median of the 5 fastest of 200 iterations, run in bursts of 20 after 250 ms idle. It also reports MSMF (maximum sustainable matmul FLOPS): the best rate held for 2 s under continuous load. It times each `torch.mm` with GPU events recorded just before and after the call, so its rates count kernel time only.
- `jax_matmul.py` (JAX 0.11.0) times `jax.jit(jnp.matmul)` with XLA autotuning on: 1 s of warmup, then the median of ten 0.2 s windows of back-to-back calls. It runs under `rocprofv3 --kernel-trace` and reports two rates per shape. Kernel time divides the FLOPs by the GPU time of the kernels inside each window, which matches MAMF-finder's timing. Wall clock divides them by host time, which also counts host dispatch and the idle GPU time between calls. Both are sustained rates, so MSMF is the PyTorch number to compare with.

An earlier version of this comment read the 2-23% wall-clock gap as XLA choosing slower kernels. Most of that gap was the timing method. Wall clock counts host dispatch and the GPU's idle time between calls: on MI350X a trivial jitted op takes about 43 µs to dispatch, and the GPU idles about 12-15 µs between executions even when the host keeps ahead (job 454529). Kernel time removes that overhead. On 2048x4096x4096 it moves JAX from 77% to 89% of MSMF, and on 4096x4096x8192 from 92% to 97%. JAX's kernels are within 4% of MSMF on four shapes. Two gaps remain: 17 points on 4608x4096x7168 and 11 points on 2048x4096x4096. TunableOp picked a rocBLAS solution for both. It samples `amdsmi` GPU 0, but HIP device 0 on k007-002 is PCI 0000:77:00, which is `amd-smi` GPU 3; `amd-smi` GPU 0 is an idle GPU at about 308 W. The MI350X MAMF and MSMF runs (jobs 453328 and 453329) predate the fix in stas00/ml-engineering#143, so their power and clock readings, the 38 MHz and 308 W in their logs, and the "not a boost burst" warning from the MAMF boost check all come from that idle GPU. Against that power-limited peak, MSMF is about 86%, JAX by kernel time on the same shape (1,189 in job 454577) about 81%, and JAX by untraced wall clock in job 453523 (1,145 TFLOP/s) 78%. MAMF's short bursts may run above the sustained clock before the GPU reaches its power limit, so the 1,400 MHz figure does not bound MAMF.

- Next: measure a training step with `--xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=false` to see whether the faster hipBLASLt kernels for the k and v GEMMs carry over. Separately, check whether XLA can use the rocBLAS solutions TunableOp picked for 4608x4096x7168 and 2048x4096x4096 (`tunableop-*.csv` in the results directory), and whether those solutions close the remaining gaps.

  | Layout | w13 | w2 |
  |---|---|---|
  | fwd | 583 → 722 | 555 → 667 |
  | dlhs | 554 → 760 | 538 → 757 |
  | drhs | 410 → 581 | 396 → 573 |

  A dense `jnp.matmul` of the same FLOPs runs at about 925–958; XLA fp16 `ragged_dot` at 24–98. At batch 8 the forward pass goes from 2.27 ms to 0.36 ms. Jobs 453500 and 453564.

- `plgpu.CompilerParams` exposes only `num_warps` and `num_stages`, so AMD knobs (`waves_per_eu`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, `kpack`) can't be set from Pallas.
- drhs, at 573–581 TFLOP/s, is the remaining gap. Both of its operands are contraction-strided.
